evaluated.name: PhysicalExpansionInNonInnovators
evaluated.hypothesis: The negative return consequence of physical capacity expansion applies mainly to firms with negligible R&D intensity; for research-intensive firms, plant growth accompanies innovation commercialization and carries no such penalty.
evaluated.reasoning: The indicator switches on only when R&D-to-sales is below 2%, so the signal is capacity growth restricted to non-innovative firms and zero elsewhere, an explicitly conditional interaction rather than a blended score. Non-innovators expanding plant are the most likely to be chasing commoditized capacity with low marginal returns, so the negative slope should be steeper than for unconditional PPE growth.
evaluated.author: proposer

evaluated.name: TangibilityWeightedCapacityGrowth
evaluated.hypothesis: The return penalty for physical capacity expansion is proportional to how purely tangible the firm's capital base is; the same rate of plant growth carries no penalty when it sits on top of a large stock of booked and internally generated intangible capital.
evaluated.reasoning: Instead of averaging two anomaly legs, the expansion rate is multiplied by the firm's tangible-capital share rank, so the signal is large and positive only for fast-expanding, intangible-poor firms and mechanically collapses toward zero for fast-expanding, intangible-rich firms. This makes the intangible dimension a slope modifier on the investment effect rather than an additive second bet, and coalescing R&D and booked intangibles to zero keeps the non-reporting cohort in coverage.
evaluated.author: proposer

evaluated.name: ExternalCapitalRaisedByNonInnovators
evaluated.expression: MUL(RATIO(ADD(sstk, DELTA(dltt, 1)), at), RANK(NEG(RATIO(ADD(COALESCE(xrd, 0), COALESCE(xad, 0)), sale))))
evaluated.hypothesis: External financing predicts low returns mainly when the firm has no intangible-investment program to justify the capital raise; issuance by R&D- and brand-building firms funds financially constrained intangible projects and should not be penalized.
evaluated.reasoning: The issuance intensity is multiplied by a continuous rank of intangible-spending deficit, so the signal loads only on capital raised by firms that spend nothing on knowledge or brand, making the intangible theme a slope modifier rather than a second additive anomaly leg. Both xrd and xad are coalesced to zero so the target cohort of non-reporters is retained, and the continuous weighting avoids the hard threshold used in the accepted capacity-growth signal.
evaluated.author: proposer

evaluated.name: BuyVersusBuildInnovation
evaluated.hypothesis: Firms that acquire their intangible capability instead of developing it internally pay market prices (and integration costs) for knowledge assets, so a buy-tilted innovation strategy predicts lower returns than an equally sized build-tilted strategy.
evaluated.reasoning: The ratio holds total innovation-directed spending roughly fixed and varies only its sourcing, so it is a genuine mix interaction rather than a rescaled acquisition-intensity (aqc/assets) variable that would simply reproduce the external-growth leg of asset growth. Both tails are meaningful — serial acquirers with no R&D at one end, pure internal innovators at the other — which should give a better-behaved long-short portfolio than the multiplicative constructions.
evaluated.author: proposer

evaluated.name: PlantTiltTrendOfCapitalStock
evaluated.hypothesis: Firms whose capital stock is drifting steadily toward plant and away from knowledge and other intangible capital are progressively locking themselves into replicable, low-option-value capacity, and this multi-year strategic drift is priced only slowly.
evaluated.reasoning: The archived TangibilityWeightedCapacityGrowth had a strongly negative FMB slope but a positive FF5 alpha, which is exactly what happens when a signal is essentially a level-of-investment sort: CMA absorbs and can over-correct the expansion leg, leaving a perverse residual. This replacement abandons the two-leg multiplicative form entirely and sorts on the five-year trend in the plant-versus-knowledge composition of the capital stock, which holds total capital growth roughly fixed and is therefore much less collinear with the investment factor while still testing the tangible-versus-intangible mechanism.
evaluated.author: proposer

evaluated.name: RevenueDeliveredPerTotalInvestmentDollar
evaluated.hypothesis: What matters is not how much a firm invests but how much output it gets per dollar deployed across all channels; firms generating large revenue gains per combined dollar of capex, R&D and advertising have genuinely productive projects, while firms deploying large tangible and intangible budgets with no revenue response are over-investing.
evaluated.reasoning: This replaces a monotone re-scaling of R&D intensity (which was mostly an industry membership sort with a mass point at zero R&D) with an investment-efficiency measure in which tangible and intangible spending enter the same denominator, so the ranking is driven by realized productivity rather than by sector. Because both high- and low-R&D firms can sit at either extreme, the sort is not a sector bet, and winsorizing at 1% controls the small-denominator tail.
evaluated.author: proposer

evaluated.name: InventoryBuildPerGrossProfit
evaluated.hypothesis: Physical working-capital expansion is only justified when the firm has intangible pricing power to sell the goods; firms accumulating inventory that is large relative to their gross profit lack product differentiation and will later face markdowns and demand disappointment.
evaluated.reasoning: This abandons the hiring channel and its contested sign, and instead scales a purely physical investment flow by gross profit, the accounting footprint of brand and product intangibles, so the same inventory build is penalized in commodity producers and tolerated in differentiated firms. Both tails are populated by real cohorts (over-stocking low-margin manufacturers versus high-margin firms with lean inventories), and the measure is a composition variable rather than a level of total investment, so it should not be neutralized by CMA.
evaluated.author: proposer

evaluated.name: GoodwillAtRiskFromRevenueDecline
evaluated.hypothesis: Purchased intangible capital only holds its book value if the acquired business keeps growing; firms whose capital base is dominated by goodwill rather than plant and whose revenue is contracting carry unrecognized impairment risk that the market prices with a lag.
evaluated.reasoning: This is a new economic channel rather than another version of the R&D share of the investment budget: it gates goodwill-heaviness of the capital stock on revenue deterioration, so the signal only fires for acquisition-built firms whose top line is failing to validate the purchase price. Firms with no goodwill sit at zero by construction, which is economically correct here because they have no impairment exposure, and the extreme values identify precisely the pre-writedown cohort.
evaluated.author: proposer

evaluated.name: NormalizedKnowledgeForPlantSubstitution
evaluated.hypothesis: The direction in which a firm reallocates its marginal investment dollar — toward knowledge capital and away from net plant — is informative about future returns independently of the size of either flow, because the R&D leg is expensed and the plant leg is capitalized.
evaluated.reasoning: Dividing by the sum of absolute changes fixes the flagged scale problem directly: the index is bounded in [-1, 1] and gives the two channels equal weight, so its variance can no longer be dominated by the mechanically larger change in net PPE. It therefore measures substitution direction rather than being a sign-flipped physical-investment sort, and it is by construction close to scale- and industry-neutral.
evaluated.author: proposer

evaluated.name: AcquiredShareOfThreeYearInvestment
evaluated.hypothesis: Holding the size of the three-year investment program fixed, the fraction executed by buying other firms rather than building plant and knowledge internally predicts lower returns, because acquired capability is paid for at market prices while internally built capital is acquired at cost.
evaluated.reasoning: This repairs the two defects that broke BuyVersusBuildInnovation's cross-sectional slope: aqc is coalesced to zero (missing acquisition spend is economically "no acquisitions", not a missing observation) and three-year sums plus a capex leg smooth the lumpiness that pushed observations onto the 0/1 boundaries, so coverage should roughly double and the ranking becomes continuous. The mechanism is unchanged from the one construction that produced a reliable FF5 alpha, so this is a targeted attempt to make the FMB and portfolio evidence agree.
evaluated.author: proposer

evaluated.name: AcquirerYearsMinusInnovatorYears
evaluated.hypothesis: What is priced is the firm's persistent growth strategy, not any single year's spending: serial acquirers who repeatedly buy capability and never sustain a research program underperform firms that show a persistent commitment to internal knowledge investment.
evaluated.reasoning: Counting the number of years out of five in which the firm was a material acquirer versus a material R&D spender converts both channels into commensurable, unit-free frequencies, so neither leg's dollar magnitude can dominate the other — the flaw that made the earlier substitution numerator a disguised PPE-change sort. It also tests a distinct mechanism, strategy persistence rather than current-year mix, and its discrete support spreads firms across many populated buckets rather than boundary spikes.
evaluated.author: proposer

evaluated.name: BoughtVersusBuiltCapitalBase
evaluated.hypothesis: The share of a firm's economic capital that was purchased at a premium (goodwill) rather than built through cumulative capex and research reflects capital acquired above replacement cost, and such capital generates lower future returns and carries impairment exposure.
evaluated.reasoning: This is the stock counterpart to Signal 1's flow mix, so the pair identifies whether the buy-versus-build effect is a slow-moving balance-sheet state or a recent-transaction effect — a cleaner test than the archived goodwill signal, which failed on the FMB side because it multiplied goodwill share by a noisy revenue-growth gate. Goodwill is coalesced to zero because absence of goodwill genuinely means no purchased capital, and the denominator's organic investment stock keeps the ratio bounded and comparable across sizes.
evaluated.author: proposer

evaluated.name: PeakRelativeKnowledgeVersusPlantSpending
evaluated.hypothesis: Firms sustaining knowledge investment at its own five-year peak while physical investment has fallen well below its peak are reallocating toward intangible capital, and because the R&D leg is expensed while the retrenched capex leg looks like contraction, the market underreacts to the transition.
evaluated.reasoning: Normalizing each channel by its own five-year maximum puts both legs on a common [0,1] scale, which repairs both failures of the earlier substitution index: the variance can no longer be dominated by the larger physical flow, and the signal varies continuously instead of collapsing onto ±1 and producing an undefined long-short spread. The distance-from-own-peak construction is also a new mechanism in the archive — it measures retrenchment relative to a firm's own history rather than cross-sectional intensity, so it is close to industry- and scale-neutral.
evaluated.author: proposer

evaluated.name: CapacityPushAgainstMarginErosion
evaluated.hypothesis: Capacity expansion is only justified when the product-market rents that intangible advantages generate are holding up; a firm pushing physical investment to the top of its own five-year range while its gross margin sits at the bottom of its own five-year range is expanding into a commoditizing business and will disappoint.
evaluated.reasoning: Both legs are within-firm time-series percentile positions, which removes the cross-sectional level of capex intensity and the cross-sectional level of gross profitability — precisely the two published anomaly components the critic identified in the ratio form — leaving only the timing interaction between capacity investment and margin erosion. Because the construct is a difference of two [0,1] own-history ranks, it is scale-, industry- and level-neutral, so it cannot be mechanically absorbed by CMA or RMW, and both tails are populated by real cohorts (expanding commoditizers versus retrenching margin-improvers).
evaluated.author: proposer

evaluated.name: ShiftTowardBuyingCapability
evaluated.hypothesis: A firm that is actively shifting its investment program away from building plant and knowledge internally toward buying capability is making a strategy change that the market prices slowly, and such shifts predict lower returns beyond the standing level of acquisitiveness.
evaluated.reasoning: This abandons the gross-profit-scaling family entirely and instead isolates one specific design choice within the only mechanism in the archive that produced a reliable FF5 alpha: whether the buy-versus-build effect is a stable firm characteristic (level, tested by the accepted Signal 1) or a transition that arrives as news (change, tested here). Because it is a one-year change in a bounded three-year mix, it is not a function of R&D-reporting status the way the flagged capex-minus-R&D construction was, it retains full coverage through the coalesced acquisition and R&D legs, and a shift in mix leaves total investment scale roughly unchanged so it stays distinct from the level-of-investment sorts CMA neutralizes.
evaluated.author: proposer

evaluated.name: KnowledgeVersusPlantInvestmentTiming
evaluated.hypothesis: Among firms that run research programs, those currently at a five-year high in research intensity while physical investment sits at a five-year low are reallocating toward knowledge capital, and because the research leg is expensed while the retrenched capex leg reads as contraction, the market underreacts.
evaluated.reasoning: This applies the winning own-history-rank construction to the two investment channels directly, so both legs are [0,1] within-firm percentiles and neither dollar magnitude nor industry membership can dominate — the flaw that broke the earlier difference-in-changes substitution index. Using xrd uncoalesced deliberately restricts the sample to innovators, which removes the R&D-reporting-status contamination the critic identified in the peak-relative and count-based signals, so the sort is a genuine intra-firm reallocation test.
evaluated.author: proposer

evaluated.name: InventoryBuildAgainstMarginErosion
evaluated.hypothesis: Physical stock-building is only warranted when the firm's product differentiation is intact; a firm whose inventory relative to sales is at a five-year high precisely when its gross margin is at a five-year low is pushing goods into a market that is no longer paying for them, and future markdowns follow.
evaluated.reasoning: This moves the winning timing-contrast construction to the working-capital channel, which was the other flow signal with a real FMB slope (InventoryBuildPerGrossProfit, fmb −3.0), while eliminating the objection that a level ratio of capex to gross profit is a mechanical quotient of two published anomalies — both legs here are own-history ranks, so cross-sectional inventory intensity and cross-sectional gross profitability are differenced out. Testing plant and inventory under identical construction tells us whether the mechanism is capacity-specific or a general physical-overexpansion-into-commoditization effect.
evaluated.author: proposer

evaluated.name: InvestmentMixInstability
evaluated.hypothesis: A firm that keeps swinging the split of its investment budget between plant and research lacks a stable strategy or is financially constrained into stop-start project funding, and such instability in intangible commitment destroys the option value of research and predicts low returns.
evaluated.reasoning: This is a second-moment mechanism entirely absent from the archive: the signal is zero-information about the *level* of either investment channel and only measures the stability of their mix, so it is orthogonal to CMA, to R&D intensity, and to the timing contrasts elsewhere in this batch. Restricting to firms reporting both capex and R&D keeps the ratio well defined and avoids the degenerate zero-volatility mass that coalescing would create for non-innovators.
evaluated.author: proposer

evaluated.name: AcquisitionSourcingRankVersusResearchSourcingRank
evaluated.hypothesis: Firms that have sourced their capability over the past five years mainly by purchasing companies rather than by funding internal research have paid market prices for intangibles, and this cumulative sourcing tilt predicts lower returns than an equally sized internally funded program.
evaluated.reasoning: The flagged version differenced two at-scaled cumulative intensities with very unequal dispersion, so it degenerated into minus R&D intensity; rank-standardizing each leg before differencing forces the two channels to contribute equally, which is the minimal change that actually identifies the sourcing mix. The two legs are not independent bets but two mutually exclusive ways of buying the same thing — capability — so their rank difference is a composition measure, and it isolates the continuous-intensity design choice against the archived binary year-count version that produced a −5.5% alpha with a flat FMB slope.
evaluated.author: proposer

evaluated.name: GoodwillOverhangWithRealInvestmentRetreat
evaluated.hypothesis: Acquired intangible capital is impaired in economic terms when it stops generating rents; firms whose goodwill is at a five-year high relative to the gross profit it produces, while their physical reinvestment rate is at a five-year low, are harvesting rather than sustaining acquired businesses and face writedowns and disappointment.
evaluated.reasoning: Scaling goodwill by gross profit rather than by net plant removes the mechanical upward drift the critic identified — goodwill over plant rises automatically because plant depreciates, whereas goodwill over gross profit rises only when acquisitions fail to deliver rents, so the own-history rank is no longer pinned at its maximum with ties. Replacing the margin leg with the firm's own physical reinvestment rank also means the signal is no longer approximately the negative of a profitability-timing rank, so it tests acquired-capital overhang jointly with real-investment retreat rather than re-testing margin deterioration.
evaluated.author: proposer

evaluated.name: LaborProductivityGainWithoutCapitalDeepening
evaluated.hypothesis: Firms whose revenue per employee is climbing to own-history highs without any corresponding deepening of physical capital per employee are generating output from intangible sources — process knowledge, brand, software, organizational capital — and this unrecorded capital formation is underpriced.
evaluated.reasoning: This introduces the labor channel, which the archive has never successfully used, and frames intangible capital formation as productivity that appears without capital deepening rather than as reported R&D, so it is defined for non-R&D-reporting firms and escapes the reporting-status contamination that has weakened several earlier signals. Both legs are own-history ranks on the same employee base, so the signal is scale-, industry- and level-neutral by construction.
evaluated.author: proposer

evaluated.name: JointCapacityAndInventoryOvercommitment
evaluated.expression: SUB(MIN(TS_RANK(RATIO(capx, MA(ppent, 3)), 5), TS_RANK(RATIO(invt, MA(sale, 3)), 5)), TS_RANK(RATIO(SUB(sale, cogs), sale), 5))
evaluated.hypothesis: Physical over-commitment is only decisive when it happens in both channels at once: a firm simultaneously at own-history highs in fixed-capacity reinvestment and in inventory relative to sales, while its gross margin sits at an own-history low, is expanding a business whose intangible pricing power is disappearing.
evaluated.reasoning: Replacing the additive stack with MIN of the two physical legs implements the conjunction the hypothesis actually states — the signal is high only if capacity *and* inventory commitment are both elevated — and the margin leg now enters exactly once, so the construction is no longer dominated by own-history margin reversal. This is a functional-form change rather than a recombination: firms high on only one physical channel are pulled down to their weaker leg instead of being averaged into the top bucket.
evaluated.author: proposer

evaluated.name: ResearchPivotDuringMarginCompression
evaluated.expression: MIN(TS_RANK(RATIO(xrd, ADD(capx, xrd)), 5), TS_RANK(NEG(RATIO(SUB(sale, cogs), sale)), 5))
evaluated.hypothesis: Innovators that pivot their investment budget toward research at the moment their margins are most compressed are adapting to competitive erosion by rebuilding intangible advantage, and this conjunction of pressure and reallocation is rewarded.
evaluated.reasoning: Using MIN instead of a rank difference removes the sign contradiction the critic identified: the margin leg no longer enters additively with the same coefficient it carries in the negatively signed capacity signal, and the signal only fires when both conditions hold, which is the conditional mechanism the hypothesis describes. The R&D-reporter restriction is deliberate rather than incidental — the hypothesis is about how an existing research program is redirected — and the archive shows this subsample can still deliver a strong cross-sectional slope (KnowledgeVersusPlantInvestmentTiming, fmb 3.85 at 0.06 coverage).
evaluated.author: proposer

evaluated.name: SlowMovingCapacityOvercommitment
evaluated.hypothesis: Over-commitment to physical capacity in the face of eroding product-market rents is a multi-year state rather than a single-year coincidence: firms whose three-year cumulative capacity spending is at an own-history high while their three-year average gross margin is at an own-history low are the ones that will disappoint.
evaluated.reasoning: This abandons the cumulative capex-versus-R&D stack the critic rejected as two published anomalies added together, and instead isolates a specific design choice on the archive's best signal — measurement horizon — by smoothing both legs to three years while keeping the own-history-rank machinery. If the horizon-smoothed version strengthens the alpha and Sharpe, the mechanism is persistent strategic over-commitment; if it weakens, the effect is genuinely a one-year timing coincidence, and either outcome sharpens the remaining generations at full coverage.
evaluated.author: proposer

evaluated.name: CapacityAdditionAgainstRentYieldOnPlant
evaluated.hypothesis: Capacity additions destroy value when each existing unit of plant is generating unusually little gross profit: the rent yield on physical capacity, which is determined by intangible advantages such as brand, product design and process knowledge, tells the firm whether more plant is worth building.
evaluated.reasoning: This repairs both flagged defects: the second leg is now gross profit per unit of plant, an explicitly intangible-rent measure built from sale and cogs, so the signal is genuinely cross-theme, and the investment leg is scaled by average assets rather than by plant, so heavy capex no longer mechanically raises one leg while depressing the other. It is distinct from the archived margin-timing signal because it conditions on the *level of rents earned per unit of capacity* rather than on the margin rate, separating rent scarcity from price erosion.
evaluated.author: proposer

evaluated.name: PivotFromBoughtToBuiltAfterWritedown
evaluated.hypothesis: Firms that have just shrunk their goodwill — through impairment or divestiture of acquired businesses — while simultaneously ramping organic investment in plant and research to own-history highs are pivoting from buying capability to building it, and the market underreacts to this strategic reversal because the writedown dominates reported earnings.
evaluated.reasoning: This is not a re-signing of the goodwill-overhang construction: the acquired-capital leg is now the *change* in goodwill (a realized writedown or disposal event) rather than its level relative to gross profit, and the investment leg is an organic-investment *ramp* rather than a retreat, so the identified cohort is the opposite one. The MIN form requires both conditions jointly, giving a clean post-impairment reallocation cohort whose positive expected sign follows from earnings-based underreaction rather than from the earlier weak contrary result.
evaluated.author: proposer

evaluated.name: BrandPushVersusCapacityPush
evaluated.hypothesis: Among firms that advertise, those currently pushing brand investment to an own-history high while physical capacity spending sits at an own-history low are building customer-based intangible capital instead of replicable plant, and this reallocation is underpriced because advertising is fully expensed.
evaluated.reasoning: Advertising is the one intangible channel in the resource menu the archive has never tested on its own, and the brand-versus-plant contrast is economically distinct from the research-versus-plant contrast because brand capital depreciates faster and pays off in demand rather than in product capability. The construction reuses the validated own-history-rank machinery so the result is interpretable against the existing family, and any positive finding would extend the theme's central claim beyond R&D.
evaluated.author: proposer

evaluated.name: RentPerWorkerVersusCapitalPerWorker
evaluated.hypothesis: Firms whose gross profit per employee is climbing to own-history highs without any deepening of plant per employee are earning rents from organizational and knowledge capital that never appears on the balance sheet, and this unrecorded capital formation is underpriced.
evaluated.reasoning: The accepted labor signal produced a strong cross-sectional slope (fmb 3.57) but no alpha, which is the signature of a revenue-scale confound; replacing revenue per worker with *gross profit* per worker isolates rent generation rather than sales volume, and gross profitability is the margin concept that has driven every successful signal in this archive. This is a single, targeted scaling change that identifies whether the labor channel's information is about intangible rents or merely about growth.
evaluated.author: proposer

evaluated.name: TotalPhysicalCommitmentAgainstMarginErosion
evaluated.expression: SUB(TS_RANK(RATIO(ADD(capx, DELTA(invt, 1)), MA(at, 3)), 5), TS_RANK(RATIO(SUB(sale, cogs), sale), 5))
evaluated.hypothesis: The economically relevant quantity is total dollars committed to physical assets — new plant plus incremental inventory — relative to the firm's size, and committing an own-history-high share of assets to hard assets while gross margin is at an own-history low predicts low returns.
evaluated.reasoning: The archive contains a rank-conjunction of the capacity and inventory channels (MIN form, alpha −2.3%) but never their economically natural dollar sum, which weights each channel by how much capital it actually absorbs rather than by percentile position and avoids the double-counted margin leg the critic rejected. Scaling by average assets rather than by plant also breaks the shared-denominator artifact present in the capex-over-plant leg, so this is a substantive measurement improvement rather than a recombination.
evaluated.author: proposer

evaluated.name: AcquisitiveNonInnovatorsOvercommittingNow
evaluated.expression: MIN(RANK(SUB(TS_RANK(RATIO(capx, MA(ppent, 3)), 5), TS_RANK(RATIO(SUB(sale, cogs), sale), 5))), MIN(RANK(TS_SUM(RATIO(COALESCE(aqc, 0), at), 5)), RANK(NEG(TS_SUM(RATIO(COALESCE(xrd, 0), at), 5)))))
evaluated.hypothesis: The worst-positioned firms satisfy three conditions at once — they have bought capability rather than built it over five years, they have no research base, and they are right now pushing physical capacity while their gross margin sits at an own-history low.
evaluated.reasoning: Replacing the additive SUMRANK with a nested MIN over three cross-sectionally ranked legs implements the conjunction the hypothesis states: a firm scores high only if it is simultaneously acquisitive, research-poor and currently over-committing, so the top bucket is a genuinely intersected cohort rather than an average of two validated sorts. Putting all three legs on the same [0,1] cross-sectional rank scale also fixes the scale-mixing problem, and coverage remains near 0.12 because every leg is defined for non-R&D reporters.
evaluated.author: proposer

evaluated.name: OvercommitmentWhereKnowledgeEndowmentIsAbsent
evaluated.expression: MIN(RANK(SUB(TS_RANK(RATIO(capx, MA(ppent, 3)), 5), TS_RANK(RATIO(SUB(sale, cogs), sale), 5))), IND_RANK(NEG(RATIO(COALESCE(xrd, 0), MA(sale, 3)))))
evaluated.hypothesis: Pushing capacity into eroding margins is punished mainly when the firm has no knowledge endowment relative to its own industry peers, because a research base offers an alternative route back to rents while a purely hard-asset firm can only compete on price.
evaluated.reasoning: The MIN form makes the knowledge-endowment leg a genuine gate rather than an additive term, so the signal fires only for firms that are simultaneously over-committing and research-poor, which is what the hypothesis claims. Using IND_RANK rather than a plain cross-sectional rank strips out the sector-level component that constitutes the published R&D-intensity anomaly, leaving within-industry knowledge poverty as the conditioning variable, and it puts the gate on the same [0,1] scale as the ranked timing contrast.
evaluated.author: proposer

evaluated.name: OvercommitmentFundedFromOutsideCapital
evaluated.expression: MIN(RANK(SUB(TS_RANK(RATIO(capx, MA(ppent, 3)), 5), TS_RANK(RATIO(SUB(sale, cogs), sale), 5))), RANK(WINSOR(RATIO(ADD(sstk, DELTA(dltt, 1)), ADD(capx, COALESCE(xrd, 0))), 1)))
evaluated.hypothesis: Capacity expansion into eroding margins is destructive specifically when the money comes from outside investors rather than from the firm's own cash generation, because external funding severs the discipline that a shrinking rent base would otherwise impose on the investment decision.
evaluated.reasoning: Two changes address the critique: the financing leg is now a *funding-mix ratio* — outside capital raised per dollar of total investment spending, including the knowledge-investment channel — rather than an issuance level, so it is not the net-external-financing anomaly in disguise, and the legs are combined with MIN so the signal fires only under the joint condition the hypothesis specifies. Both legs are cross-sectional ranks in [0,1], and winsorizing the funding ratio controls the small-denominator tail for firms with negligible investment.
evaluated.author: proposer

evaluated.name: KnowledgeRichCapitalRestraintWithMarginRepair
evaluated.expression: MUL(RANK(SUB(TS_RANK(RATIO(SUB(sale, cogs), sale), 5), TS_RANK(RATIO(capx, MA(ppent, 3)), 5))), IND_RANK(RATIO(COALESCE(xrd, 0), MA(sale, 3))))
evaluated.hypothesis: The long side of the theme is the mirror image of the short side: firms whose gross margins are at own-history highs while physical capital commitment is at own-history lows, and which carry a strong research base relative to peers, are compounding intangible advantage without absorbing capital, and this is underpriced.
evaluated.reasoning: Every strong result in this archive is on the short side, and the positive-signed candidates (PeakRelative at t 1.78, KnowledgeVersusPlantTiming with no alpha) were never given the gating structure that made the short side work, so this tests whether the conjunction mechanism is symmetric or whether the effect is purely a distress/over-commitment phenomenon. It keeps full coverage through the zero-R&D convention and the industry-relative endowment gate, so a positive result would not be a repackaged R&D-intensity sort.
evaluated.author: proposer

evaluated.name: CapacityPushIntoDeterioratingRentTrend
evaluated.hypothesis: What matters for capacity decisions is the direction in which the firm's intangible pricing power is moving, not merely where the current margin sits in its own history: committing capital while the five-year margin trend is steeply negative signals expansion into structural competitive decline.
evaluated.reasoning: Every successful signal in the archive uses the *position* of the margin in its own five-year history, which conflates cyclical dips with structural erosion; substituting a five-year fitted margin trend tests whether the mechanism is about direction of decline, and if so this variant should improve both the slope and the alpha because it removes mean-reverting margin noise from the gate. The capex leg stays as an own-history rank so no cross-sectional investment level enters, keeping the construct outside CMA's span.
evaluated.author: proposer

evaluated.name: NetHardAssetCommitmentAgainstMarginErosion
evaluated.expression: SUB(TS_RANK(RATIO(SUB(capx, COALESCE(xrd, 0)), MA(at, 3)), 5), TS_RANK(RATIO(SUB(sale, cogs), sale), 5))
evaluated.hypothesis: What is punished is hard-asset accumulation *net of* knowledge accumulation: a firm putting an own-history-high share of its asset base into plant beyond what it spends on research, precisely while gross margin sits at an own-history low, is deepening a commoditizing business instead of renewing its advantage.
evaluated.reasoning: Rather than smoothing an existing gate, this moves the intangible channel inside the commitment measure itself: the investment leg is now a signed tangible-minus-knowledge spending balance, so the same firm is scored differently depending on whether its capex is accompanied by research, which is the theme's mechanism expressed continuously rather than as an extreme-cohort intersection. It keeps full coverage through the zero-R&D convention, scales by average assets so the two channels are commensurable, and remains a within-firm timing contrast that no cross-sectional investment factor spans.
evaluated.author: proposer

evaluated.name: LeveragingUpWhileStarvingIntangibles
evaluated.expression: SUB(TS_RANK(RATIO(DELTA(ADD(dltt, dlc), 1), MA(at, 3)), 5), TS_RANK(RATIO(ADD(COALESCE(xrd, 0), COALESCE(xad, 0)), MA(sale, 3)), 5))
evaluated.hypothesis: Firms adding debt at an own-history-high rate while cutting research and brand spending to own-history lows are financing current obligations by mortgaging their intangible future, and this substitution of leverage for intangible investment predicts low returns.
evaluated.reasoning: This abandons the funding-gate construction entirely and pairs the financing channel directly against the intangible-spending channel, both as own-history ranks, so it tests a distinct economic mechanism — debt-for-intangibles substitution — rather than re-aggregating the archived capacity-timing legs. Coverage stays full because both intangible spending items are coalesced to zero under the standard non-reporting convention, and because neither leg is a cross-sectional level the construct is not the leverage or issuance anomaly.
evaluated.author: proposer

evaluated.name: InnovatorPivotingToAcquiredCapability
evaluated.hypothesis: Among firms that actually run research programs, those whose acquisition spending has climbed to an own-history high while their research intensity has fallen to an own-history low are substituting purchased capability for internal capability, and this within-firm pivot predicts low returns.
evaluated.reasoning: The archive's buy-versus-build evidence is entirely cross-sectional, which is precisely why it yields large alphas with no cross-sectional slope — the level of acquisitiveness is a sticky firm characteristic. Recasting buy-versus-build as a *within-firm timing* contrast on the same asset scale, in the subsample where both channels are genuinely available, tests whether the pivot itself carries information, and it avoids the extreme-cohort concentration problem the critic identified in stacked rank products.
evaluated.author: proposer

evaluated.name: TotalCapitalAbsorptionAgainstRentMomentum
evaluated.expression: SUB(TS_RANK(RATIO(ADD(ADD(capx, COALESCE(xrd, 0)), DELTA(invt, 1)), MA(at, 3)), 5), TS_RANK(GROWTH(SUB(sale, cogs), 1), 5))
evaluated.hypothesis: If the over-commitment effect is specific to tangible investment, then a commitment measure that also counts knowledge spending should predict returns more weakly: total capital absorption at an own-history high while gross-profit growth is at an own-history low should be a materially softer negative signal than its tangible-only counterpart.
evaluated.reasoning: This replaces the rejected gross-profitability placebo gate with a cleaner adjudication of the theme's central claim: the intangible channel enters by being *added into* the commitment measure rather than by gating it, and the rent leg is switched from margin level to gross-profit growth so the margin term is not double-counted. Comparing its strength against the tangible-only signals tells us directly whether the archive's alphas come from tangible over-commitment or from capital absorption generally, which is decisive information for the final generations.
evaluated.author: proposer

evaluated.name: CapitalRestraintGatedByKnowledgeStockShare
evaluated.expression: MUL(RANK(SUB(TS_RANK(RATIO(SUB(sale, cogs), sale), 5), TS_RANK(RATIO(capx, MA(ppent, 3)), 5))), IND_RANK(RATIO(TS_SUM(COALESCE(xrd, 0), 3), ADD(ppent, TS_SUM(COALESCE(xrd, 0), 3)))))
evaluated.hypothesis: The long-side effect operates through the composition of the firm's accumulated capital — knowledge stock relative to physical stock — rather than through the level of its current research spending: capital-light firms repairing margins pay off most when their capital base is already knowledge-weighted.
evaluated.reasoning: The archive's best positive signal gated on industry-relative R&D-to-sales, which the critic correctly noted cannot be separated from the published R&D-intensity anomaly; replacing that gate with an industry-relative *capital-composition* measure tests the same economic claim with a variable that is a stock mix rather than a spending intensity. If the joint evidence survives the substitution, the mechanism is genuinely about intangible capital composition, which is exactly the theme's claim and the most valuable thing to establish before the final generations.
evaluated.author: proposer

evaluated.name: SignedRestraintInteractionWithKnowledgeEndowment
evaluated.expression: MUL(SUB(TS_RANK(RATIO(SUB(sale, cogs), sale), 5), TS_RANK(RATIO(capx, MA(ppent, 3)), 5)), IND_RANK(RATIO(COALESCE(xrd, 0), MA(sale, 3))))
evaluated.hypothesis: Knowledge endowment amplifies the return consequences of capital-allocation timing in both directions: among research-rich firms, capital restraint with margin repair is strongly rewarded and capacity pushing into margin erosion is strongly punished, while research-poor firms show a muted response either way.
evaluated.reasoning: The archive's best positive signal ranked the contrast before gating, which discards its sign and forces knowledge-poor firms to the bottom of the sort; keeping the contrast signed in [−1, 1] and multiplying by a [0, 1] endowment weight makes the construct a genuine interaction slope, with knowledge-poor firms pooled near zero in the middle and both extremes occupied by knowledge-rich firms on opposite sides of the allocation decision. This is a structural change rather than an aggregator swap, and it directly tests whether the effect is a one-sided cohort or a true amplification.
evaluated.author: proposer

evaluated.name: MaturedResearchPayoffWithCapitalRestraint
evaluated.expression: MUL(RANK(SUB(TS_RANK(RATIO(SUB(sale, cogs), MA(at, 3)), 5), TS_RANK(RATIO(capx, MA(ppent, 3)), 5))), IND_RANK(RATIO(COALESCE(LAG(xrd, 3), 0), MA(sale, 3))))
evaluated.hypothesis: Research pays off with a multi-year lag: firms whose gross profit per unit of assets is now at an own-history high while capital spending stays at an own-history low, and which were heavy researchers three years ago, are harvesting matured intangible investment that the market never capitalized.
evaluated.reasoning: Every intangible leg in the archive is contemporaneous, which conflates spending with payoff; lagging the endowment gate three years imposes the actual economics of the research-to-rent conversion and makes the long leg a harvest cohort rather than a high-spending cohort. The rent leg is also switched from margin rate to gross profit per unit of assets so the signal captures rent *scale* generated on a capital base that is not growing, and the zero convention on unreported past research keeps coverage at full sample width.
evaluated.author: proposer

evaluated.name: AcceleratingNetHardAssetCommitment
evaluated.expression: SUB(TS_RANK(ACCEL(RATIO(SUB(capx, COALESCE(xrd, 0)), MA(at, 3))), 5), TS_RANK(RATIO(SUB(sale, cogs), sale), 5))
evaluated.hypothesis: Over-commitment is most damaging when it is still accelerating: a firm whose net hard-asset commitment rate is rising at an own-history-high pace while gross margin sits at an own-history low is escalating a losing capital-allocation decision rather than merely maintaining a high level.
evaluated.reasoning: Rather than uniting two archived commitment legs, this changes the temporal content of the leg from level-in-own-history to change-in-change, which distinguishes chronic capital-heavy firms (already captured by the archive) from firms actively escalating hard-asset spending net of research — a different economic state with a different expected persistence. The rent leg and window are held fixed so the comparison against the archived level version is clean, and coverage stays at full sample width through the standard zero-research convention.
evaluated.author: proposer

evaluated.name: SignedNetCommitmentAmplifiedByKnowledgePoverty
evaluated.expression: MUL(SUB(TS_RANK(RATIO(SUB(capx, COALESCE(xrd, 0)), MA(at, 3)), 5), TS_RANK(RATIO(SUB(sale, cogs), sale), 5)), IND_RANK(NEG(RATIO(COALESCE(xrd, 0), MA(sale, 3)))))
evaluated.hypothesis: Knowledge poverty amplifies the penalty for net hard-asset over-commitment in both directions: among firms with no research base relative to peers, committing capital while margins erode is severely punished and restraint while margins repair is rewarded, whereas research-rich firms respond weakly either way.
evaluated.reasoning: This is the short-side counterpart to the accepted signed long-side interaction, and it differs structurally from every gated signal in the archive: the contrast keeps its sign in [−1, 1] instead of being pre-ranked, and the commitment leg is the netted capex-minus-research measure that preserved the cross-sectional slope where hard MIN gates destroyed it. Knowledge-rich firms are pooled near zero in the middle rather than pushed to one tail, so the sort's extremes are opposite allocation decisions by the same type of firm — a genuine amplification test rather than a cohort intersection.
evaluated.author: proposer

evaluated.name: TangibilityDriftAgainstPeersWithMarginErosion
evaluated.hypothesis: Firms whose asset base is drifting toward hard capital relative to their industry peers, at the same time as their own gross margin falls to an own-history low, are losing the intangible race in their product market and will underperform.
evaluated.reasoning: The degenerate leg is removed: industry-relative tangibility is defined for every firm from ppent and at, so no part of the sample is sorted on an industry research trend the way an industry-adjusted coalesced R&D leg would be. Economically it shifts the intangible dimension from own spending to competitive capital-structure position — the firm becoming more hard-asset-dependent than its peers while its own rents erode — which is a channel the archive has not tested and which stays a within-firm timing contrast, keeping it outside CMA and RMW.
evaluated.author: proposer

evaluated.name: MaturedKnowledgeStockHarvest
evaluated.expression: MUL(RANK(SUB(TS_RANK(RATIO(SUB(sale, cogs), MA(at, 3)), 5), TS_RANK(RATIO(capx, MA(ppent, 3)), 5))), IND_RANK(RATIO(TS_SUM(COALESCE(LAG(xrd, 2), 0), 3), MA(sale, 3))))
evaluated.hypothesis: What is harvested is a *stock* of matured research, not a single vintage: firms with high cumulative research spending from three to five years ago that are now producing rising gross profit on a static capital base are monetizing an unrecorded knowledge stock the market never capitalized.
evaluated.reasoning: If the winner's three-year lag captured a genuine conversion delay, replacing the single lagged year with the cumulative research of the three years ending three years ago should be strictly less noisy and therefore strengthen both the slope and the alpha; if it does not, the lag was picking up mean reversion in a single noisy observation. The gate stays industry-relative so sector R&D norms are removed, and coverage is unchanged at roughly 0.12 through the standard zero-research convention.
evaluated.author: proposer

evaluated.name: SignedRestraintWithMaturedResearchGate
evaluated.expression: MUL(SUB(TS_RANK(RATIO(SUB(sale, cogs), MA(at, 3)), 5), TS_RANK(RATIO(capx, MA(ppent, 3)), 5)), IND_RANK(RATIO(COALESCE(LAG(xrd, 3), 0), MA(sale, 3))))
evaluated.hypothesis: Past research endowment amplifies the return consequences of current capital allocation in both directions: among firms that were heavy researchers three years ago, rent expansion with capital restraint is strongly rewarded and rent contraction with capacity pushing is strongly punished, while firms with no research history respond weakly either way.
evaluated.reasoning: This combines the two independently best-performing design features in the archive — the signed contrast, which delivered the strongest cross-sectional slope (fmb +4.79), and the lagged research gate, which delivered the strongest alpha and Sharpe (+3.9%, 0.47) — into one construction, and it is a structural change rather than a recombination because keeping the sign places knowledge-poor firms in the middle instead of the bottom tail. It is the most likely candidate to carry both forms of evidence into the final generation.
evaluated.author: proposer

evaluated.name: ResearchCommitmentPersistenceHarvest
evaluated.expression: MUL(RANK(SUB(TS_RANK(RATIO(SUB(sale, cogs), MA(at, 3)), 5), TS_RANK(RATIO(capx, MA(ppent, 3)), 5))), IND_RANK(TS_SUM(INDICATOR(RATIO(COALESCE(xrd, 0), sale), 0.02), 5)))
evaluated.hypothesis: What creates a harvestable unrecorded knowledge stock is sustained commitment rather than the level of any single year's spending: firms that maintained material research in most of the past five years and are now producing own-history-high gross profit on a static capital base are monetizing accumulated capability the balance sheet never recorded.
evaluated.reasoning: The gate is a new economic construct for this frame — a five-year frequency of material research commitment, industry-ranked — rather than a re-timed version of research intensity, and the archive's evidence that persistence counts carried large alphas (AcquirerYearsMinusInnovatorYears) supports its relevance. It also removes a weakness of intensity gates: a single spike in R&D-to-sales caused by collapsing sales cannot qualify a firm as research-rich, which should sharpen both the slope and the portfolio composition.
evaluated.author: proposer

evaluated.name: RentYieldOnTotalCapitalIncludingKnowledge
evaluated.expression: SUB(TS_RANK(RATIO(SUB(sale, cogs), ADD(MA(ppent, 3), TS_SUM(COALESCE(LAG(xrd, 2), 0), 3))), 5), TS_RANK(RATIO(capx, MA(ppent, 3)), 5))
evaluated.hypothesis: The economically correct denominator for rent generation is physical capital plus the matured knowledge stock that produced those rents; firms whose return on this total capital base is at an own-history high while physical investment is at an own-history low are compounding intangible advantage without absorbing capital.
evaluated.reasoning: This is not an ablation of the winner but a new measurement idea: the intangible channel enters the *denominator of a rent yield* rather than as an external gate, so knowledge capital is treated as capital rather than as a firm characteristic, and the signal is defined for every firm through the standard zero-research convention. Using research lagged two to four years matches the conversion delay that the archive's lagged gate identified, and both legs stay own-history ranks so no cross-sectional profitability or investment level enters.
evaluated.author: proposer

evaluated.name: ResearchAbandonmentWhilePushingCapacity
evaluated.expression: MUL(SUB(TS_RANK(RATIO(capx, MA(ppent, 3)), 5), TS_RANK(RATIO(COALESCE(xrd, 0), MA(at, 3)), 5)), IND_RANK(RATIO(COALESCE(LAG(xrd, 3), 0), MA(sale, 3))))
evaluated.hypothesis: Former heavy researchers that have cut research to own-history lows while pushing plant spending to own-history highs are abandoning an intangible strategy in favour of replicable capacity, and this reversal of strategic direction predicts low returns.
evaluated.reasoning: This is a distinct economic state from the knowledge-poverty interaction already in the archive: the gate selects firms that *had* a research base three years ago, and the contrast then identifies those now dismantling it, so the short leg is pipeline abandonment rather than chronic hard-asset dependence. Because the gate and the current-research leg use different vintages of the same variable, the signal cannot be reproduced by a combination of the archived signed contrast and its knowledge-poverty version.
evaluated.author: proposer

evaluated.name: BuiltShareOfIntangibleBaseHarvest
evaluated.expression: MUL(RANK(SUB(TS_RANK(RATIO(SUB(sale, cogs), MA(at, 3)), 5), TS_RANK(RATIO(capx, MA(ppent, 3)), 5))), IND_RANK(RATIO(TS_SUM(COALESCE(xrd, 0), 3), ADD(TS_SUM(COALESCE(xrd, 0), 3), COALESCE(intan, 0)))))
evaluated.hypothesis: The harvest premium accrues specifically to firms whose intangible base was internally built and therefore never capitalized: among capital-light firms with rising rents, those whose knowledge capital comes from their own research rather than from acquired intangibles are the ones the market misprices.
evaluated.reasoning: The double-count is removed — the gate now contrasts cumulative research against reported intangible assets, which already subsume goodwill, so it measures the *built share* of the intangible base rather than adding goodwill twice. The prediction is a genuine positive one rather than a placebo: if unrecorded capital is the source of the mispricing, the built-share gate should be at least as strong as the raw research-intensity gate, and it delivers the built-versus-bought adjudication with an alpha-seeking sign.
evaluated.author: proposer

evaluated.name: NetCommitmentRestraintInResearchFranchises
evaluated.expression: MUL(SUB(TS_RANK(RATIO(SUB(sale, cogs), MA(at, 3)), 5), TS_RANK(RATIO(SUB(capx, COALESCE(xrd, 0)), MA(at, 3)), 5)), IND_RANK(TS_SUM(INDICATOR(RATIO(COALESCE(xrd, 0), sale), 0.02), 5)))
evaluated.hypothesis: Restraint should be measured on hard assets net of knowledge spending, so that a research franchise is not scored as profligate merely for funding research: firms whose rents are at own-history highs while net hard-asset commitment is at own-history lows, and which persistently invest in research, are the purest harvest cohort.
evaluated.reasoning: This unifies the best-validated commitment measure on the short side (capex net of research over assets, fmb −4.79, Sharpe −0.33) with the best-validated gate on the long side, correcting a real inconsistency in the current winners, whose capex-over-plant leg penalizes exactly the research-intensive firms the gate selects. Keeping the contrast signed places non-franchise firms in the middle of the sort rather than in the short tail, which is the structure that produced the archive's strongest cross-sectional slopes.
evaluated.author: proposer

evaluated.name: ScalableRentPerWorkerInResearchFranchises
evaluated.expression: MUL(RANK(SUB(TS_RANK(RATIO(SUB(sale, cogs), emp), 5), TS_RANK(RATIO(ppent, emp), 5))), IND_RANK(TS_SUM(INDICATOR(RATIO(COALESCE(xrd, 0), sale), 0.02), 5)))
evaluated.hypothesis: Rising gross profit per employee without capital deepening signals intangible-driven scalability, but it is only mispriced when the underlying capability is internally built and unrecorded; among persistent researchers this labour-productivity gain is a genuine unrecorded-capital signal rather than a cyclical revenue effect.
evaluated.reasoning: The labour channel has repeatedly produced strong cross-sectional slopes with no portfolio alpha (fmb +3.19 to +3.57, t-alpha ≈ 0.05–0.46), the signature of a signal whose extreme deciles are populated by the wrong firms; adding the research-franchise gate is the specific economic fix, since it restricts the long leg to firms whose productivity gains plausibly come from unrecorded knowledge capital. This is the one remaining untested combination that could add an economically distinct input channel — labour rather than capital — to the winning mechanism.
evaluated.author: proposer

evaluated.name: FranchiseDismantlingWhilePushingPlant
evaluated.hypothesis: The mirror of the harvest is dismantling: firms that built a persistent research franchise in earlier years but have now cut research to own-history lows while pushing plant spending to own-history highs are liquidating intangible capability in favour of replicable capacity, and this reversal predicts low returns.
evaluated.reasoning: The archived abandonment signal used a single lagged research vintage as the gate and delivered the archive's strongest short-side slope (fmb −4.86) with a modest alpha (−2.1%); replacing that gate with franchise *persistence* targets firms with a genuine multi-year research history to dismantle, which should concentrate the short leg on real strategic reversals rather than on one-off spending dips. It also completes the symmetry test of the winning mechanism using the gate construct that proved strongest on the long side.
evaluated.author: proposer

evaluated.name: TotalPhysicalRestraintHarvest
evaluated.expression: MUL(RANK(SUB(TS_RANK(RATIO(SUB(sale, cogs), MA(at, 3)), 5), TS_RANK(RATIO(ADD(capx, DELTA(invt, 1)), MA(at, 3)), 5))), IND_RANK(TS_SUM(INDICATOR(RATIO(COALESCE(xrd, 0), sale), 0.02), 5)))
evaluated.hypothesis: Genuine capital restraint means withholding dollars from every hard-asset channel, plant and working capital alike; research franchises whose rents rise while total physical commitment falls to own-history lows are the cleanest case of intangible capital doing the work.
evaluated.reasoning: The dollar-summed physical commitment measure was validated independently on the short side (fmb −4.71, alpha −2.3%) and captures firms that restrain plant while quietly building inventory, which the capex-over-plant leg misses entirely, so this is a measurement upgrade to the restraint leg rather than a re-aggregation of ranks. Combined with the persistence gate that produced the archive's best Sharpe, it is the most complete version of the mechanism this search has identified and a suitable final candidate.
evaluated.author: proposer

evaluated.name: RisingResearchFranchiseHarvest
evaluated.expression: MUL(RANK(SUB(TS_RANK(RATIO(SUB(sale, cogs), MA(at, 3)), 5), TS_RANK(RATIO(capx, MA(ppent, 3)), 5))), IND_RANK(TREND(RATIO(COALESCE(xrd, 0), MA(sale, 3)), 5)))
evaluated.hypothesis: The harvest premium is largest where the knowledge pipeline is still being expanded: firms whose research intensity has been on a rising five-year trend relative to peers, and which are now producing own-history-high rents on a static capital base, are monetizing matured research while continuing to build the next vintage, so the mispricing does not self-correct.
evaluated.reasoning: The gate content is genuinely different from every archived version — a fitted five-year *trend* in research intensity measures the direction of intangible commitment rather than its level, its persistence count, or a lagged vintage, and it distinguishes an expanding franchise from a mature one harvesting a declining pipeline. Industry-ranking the trend removes sector-wide shifts in research norms, non-reporters sit in the middle of the gate rather than at an artificial extreme, and coverage stays near the 0.12 full-sample width of the winning family.
evaluated.author: proposer

evaluated.name: FranchiseCashBuildWithCapitalRestraint
evaluated.hypothesis: Genuine intangible capital shows up as cash: persistent researchers whose cash balances are climbing to own-history highs while plant spending sits at own-history lows are converting unrecorded knowledge capital into liquidity rather than absorbing capital, and the market underprices this because the underlying asset never appears on the balance sheet.
evaluated.reasoning: This replaces the sign-flipped reallocation contrast with an entirely new outcome variable for the harvest mechanism — internal liquidity accumulation, using the one investment-menu variable (che) that this search has never employed — so it is neither a rediscovery of the abandonment signal nor the negative of any other proposal in this batch. It also tests the mechanism's economic content more directly than a rent-margin leg: if research franchises with capital restraint are truly harvesting, the cash must accumulate, and the gate ensures the long leg is built from committed innovators rather than cash-rich firms generally.
evaluated.author: proposer

considered.name: PhysicalExpansionInNonInnovators
considered.hypothesis: The negative return consequence of physical capacity expansion applies mainly to firms with negligible R&D intensity; for research-intensive firms, plant growth accompanies innovation commercialization and carries no such penalty.
considered.reasoning: The indicator switches on only when R&D-to-sales is below 2%, so the signal is capacity growth restricted to non-innovative firms and zero elsewhere, an explicitly conditional interaction rather than a blended score. Non-innovators expanding plant are the most likely to be chasing commoditized capacity with low marginal returns, so the negative slope should be steeper than for unconditional PPE growth.
considered.author: proposer

considered.name: BudgetShiftTowardKnowledgeInvestment
considered.hypothesis: A year-over-year reallocation of the total investment budget from physical capex toward R&D signals a shift into higher-return, harder-to-value projects whose payoffs are systematically underpriced.
considered.reasoning: The level of the R&D share is largely an industry fixture, but its change is a firm-specific decision about the composition of investment, mixing both themes in one state variable. Because intangible spending is expensed and depresses current earnings while tangible capex is capitalized, investors under-react to such reallocations, implying positive subsequent abnormal returns.
considered.author: proposer

considered.name: TangibilityWeightedCapacityGrowth
considered.hypothesis: The return penalty for physical capacity expansion is proportional to how purely tangible the firm's capital base is; the same rate of plant growth carries no penalty when it sits on top of a large stock of booked and internally generated intangible capital.
considered.reasoning: Instead of averaging two anomaly legs, the expansion rate is multiplied by the firm's tangible-capital share rank, so the signal is large and positive only for fast-expanding, intangible-poor firms and mechanically collapses toward zero for fast-expanding, intangible-rich firms. This makes the intangible dimension a slope modifier on the investment effect rather than an additive second bet, and coalescing R&D and booked intangibles to zero keeps the non-reporting cohort in coverage.
considered.author: proposer

considered.name: GoodwillShareOfInvestmentBudget
considered.hypothesis: Holding total investment scale fixed, the fraction of the investment budget that lands on the balance sheet as unidentifiable goodwill measures how much the firm paid above fair value for intangibles it could not build internally, and that overpayment is not fully impounded in prices.
considered.reasoning: The denominator is total investment spending across all three channels (physical, knowledge, acquired), so the signal is a pure composition measure that is not a restatement of investment scale or of aqc/assets, removing the double-count objection. Firms whose expansion is mostly purchased goodwill rather than capex or R&D face later impairments and integration failures, while equal-scale spenders who build intangibles internally do not, giving a negative slope driven by the mix rather than the level.
considered.author: proposer

considered.name: ReportedVersusEconomicCapitalGrowthWedge
considered.hypothesis: When book asset growth outruns growth in economic capital (tangible assets plus capitalized knowledge stock), the expansion is an accounting artifact of purchased intangibles and goodwill rather than real productive capacity, and such growth predicts low returns.
considered.reasoning: Differencing the two growth measures cancels the common asset-growth component, so the signal is a wedge that is close to orthogonal to plain asset growth and to intangible-adjusted growth individually rather than a refinement of either. A positive wedge identifies firms whose balance-sheet expansion is intangible-by-acquisition while internal knowledge accumulation stagnates; a negative wedge identifies R&D-driven economic growth that reported assets understate.
considered.author: proposer

considered.name: ExternalCapitalRaisedByNonInnovators
considered.expression: MUL(RATIO(ADD(sstk, DELTA(dltt, 1)), at), RANK(NEG(RATIO(ADD(COALESCE(xrd, 0), COALESCE(xad, 0)), sale))))
considered.hypothesis: External financing predicts low returns mainly when the firm has no intangible-investment program to justify the capital raise; issuance by R&D- and brand-building firms funds financially constrained intangible projects and should not be penalized.
considered.reasoning: The issuance intensity is multiplied by a continuous rank of intangible-spending deficit, so the signal loads only on capital raised by firms that spend nothing on knowledge or brand, making the intangible theme a slope modifier rather than a second additive anomaly leg. Both xrd and xad are coalesced to zero so the target cohort of non-reporters is retained, and the continuous weighting avoids the hard threshold used in the accepted capacity-growth signal.
considered.author: proposer

considered.name: BuyVersusBuildInnovation
considered.hypothesis: Firms that acquire their intangible capability instead of developing it internally pay market prices (and integration costs) for knowledge assets, so a buy-tilted innovation strategy predicts lower returns than an equally sized build-tilted strategy.
considered.reasoning: The ratio holds total innovation-directed spending roughly fixed and varies only its sourcing, so it is a genuine mix interaction rather than a rescaled acquisition-intensity (aqc/assets) variable that would simply reproduce the external-growth leg of asset growth. Both tails are meaningful — serial acquirers with no R&D at one end, pure internal innovators at the other — which should give a better-behaved long-short portfolio than the multiplicative constructions.
considered.author: proposer

considered.name: PlantTiltTrendOfCapitalStock
considered.hypothesis: Firms whose capital stock is drifting steadily toward plant and away from knowledge and other intangible capital are progressively locking themselves into replicable, low-option-value capacity, and this multi-year strategic drift is priced only slowly.
considered.reasoning: The archived TangibilityWeightedCapacityGrowth had a strongly negative FMB slope but a positive FF5 alpha, which is exactly what happens when a signal is essentially a level-of-investment sort: CMA absorbs and can over-correct the expansion leg, leaving a perverse residual. This replacement abandons the two-leg multiplicative form entirely and sorts on the five-year trend in the plant-versus-knowledge composition of the capital stock, which holds total capital growth roughly fixed and is therefore much less collinear with the investment factor while still testing the tangible-versus-intangible mechanism.
considered.author: proposer

considered.name: RevenueDeliveredPerTotalInvestmentDollar
considered.hypothesis: What matters is not how much a firm invests but how much output it gets per dollar deployed across all channels; firms generating large revenue gains per combined dollar of capex, R&D and advertising have genuinely productive projects, while firms deploying large tangible and intangible budgets with no revenue response are over-investing.
considered.reasoning: This replaces a monotone re-scaling of R&D intensity (which was mostly an industry membership sort with a mass point at zero R&D) with an investment-efficiency measure in which tangible and intangible spending enter the same denominator, so the ranking is driven by realized productivity rather than by sector. Because both high- and low-R&D firms can sit at either extreme, the sort is not a sector bet, and winsorizing at 1% controls the small-denominator tail.
considered.author: proposer

considered.name: InventoryBuildPerGrossProfit
considered.hypothesis: Physical working-capital expansion is only justified when the firm has intangible pricing power to sell the goods; firms accumulating inventory that is large relative to their gross profit lack product differentiation and will later face markdowns and demand disappointment.
considered.reasoning: This abandons the hiring channel and its contested sign, and instead scales a purely physical investment flow by gross profit, the accounting footprint of brand and product intangibles, so the same inventory build is penalized in commodity producers and tolerated in differentiated firms. Both tails are populated by real cohorts (over-stocking low-margin manufacturers versus high-margin firms with lean inventories), and the measure is a composition variable rather than a level of total investment, so it should not be neutralized by CMA.
considered.author: proposer

considered.name: GoodwillAtRiskFromRevenueDecline
considered.hypothesis: Purchased intangible capital only holds its book value if the acquired business keeps growing; firms whose capital base is dominated by goodwill rather than plant and whose revenue is contracting carry unrecognized impairment risk that the market prices with a lag.
considered.reasoning: This is a new economic channel rather than another version of the R&D share of the investment budget: it gates goodwill-heaviness of the capital stock on revenue deterioration, so the signal only fires for acquisition-built firms whose top line is failing to validate the purchase price. Firms with no goodwill sit at zero by construction, which is economically correct here because they have no impairment exposure, and the extreme values identify precisely the pre-writedown cohort.
considered.author: proposer

considered.name: NormalizedKnowledgeForPlantSubstitution
considered.hypothesis: The direction in which a firm reallocates its marginal investment dollar — toward knowledge capital and away from net plant — is informative about future returns independently of the size of either flow, because the R&D leg is expensed and the plant leg is capitalized.
considered.reasoning: Dividing by the sum of absolute changes fixes the flagged scale problem directly: the index is bounded in [-1, 1] and gives the two channels equal weight, so its variance can no longer be dominated by the mechanically larger change in net PPE. It therefore measures substitution direction rather than being a sign-flipped physical-investment sort, and it is by construction close to scale- and industry-neutral.
considered.author: proposer

considered.name: AcquiredShareOfThreeYearInvestment
considered.hypothesis: Holding the size of the three-year investment program fixed, the fraction executed by buying other firms rather than building plant and knowledge internally predicts lower returns, because acquired capability is paid for at market prices while internally built capital is acquired at cost.
considered.reasoning: This repairs the two defects that broke BuyVersusBuildInnovation's cross-sectional slope: aqc is coalesced to zero (missing acquisition spend is economically "no acquisitions", not a missing observation) and three-year sums plus a capex leg smooth the lumpiness that pushed observations onto the 0/1 boundaries, so coverage should roughly double and the ranking becomes continuous. The mechanism is unchanged from the one construction that produced a reliable FF5 alpha, so this is a targeted attempt to make the FMB and portfolio evidence agree.
considered.author: proposer

considered.name: AcquirerYearsMinusInnovatorYears
considered.hypothesis: What is priced is the firm's persistent growth strategy, not any single year's spending: serial acquirers who repeatedly buy capability and never sustain a research program underperform firms that show a persistent commitment to internal knowledge investment.
considered.reasoning: Counting the number of years out of five in which the firm was a material acquirer versus a material R&D spender converts both channels into commensurable, unit-free frequencies, so neither leg's dollar magnitude can dominate the other — the flaw that made the earlier substitution numerator a disguised PPE-change sort. It also tests a distinct mechanism, strategy persistence rather than current-year mix, and its discrete support spreads firms across many populated buckets rather than boundary spikes.
considered.author: proposer

considered.name: BoughtVersusBuiltCapitalBase
considered.hypothesis: The share of a firm's economic capital that was purchased at a premium (goodwill) rather than built through cumulative capex and research reflects capital acquired above replacement cost, and such capital generates lower future returns and carries impairment exposure.
considered.reasoning: This is the stock counterpart to Signal 1's flow mix, so the pair identifies whether the buy-versus-build effect is a slow-moving balance-sheet state or a recent-transaction effect — a cleaner test than the archived goodwill signal, which failed on the FMB side because it multiplied goodwill share by a noisy revenue-growth gate. Goodwill is coalesced to zero because absence of goodwill genuinely means no purchased capital, and the denominator's organic investment stock keeps the ratio bounded and comparable across sizes.
considered.author: proposer

considered.name: PeakRelativeKnowledgeVersusPlantSpending
considered.hypothesis: Firms sustaining knowledge investment at its own five-year peak while physical investment has fallen well below its peak are reallocating toward intangible capital, and because the R&D leg is expensed while the retrenched capex leg looks like contraction, the market underreacts to the transition.
considered.reasoning: Normalizing each channel by its own five-year maximum puts both legs on a common [0,1] scale, which repairs both failures of the earlier substitution index: the variance can no longer be dominated by the larger physical flow, and the signal varies continuously instead of collapsing onto ±1 and producing an undefined long-short spread. The distance-from-own-peak construction is also a new mechanism in the archive — it measures retrenchment relative to a firm's own history rather than cross-sectional intensity, so it is close to industry- and scale-neutral.
considered.author: proposer

considered.name: CapacityPushAgainstMarginErosion
considered.hypothesis: Capacity expansion is only justified when the product-market rents that intangible advantages generate are holding up; a firm pushing physical investment to the top of its own five-year range while its gross margin sits at the bottom of its own five-year range is expanding into a commoditizing business and will disappoint.
considered.reasoning: Both legs are within-firm time-series percentile positions, which removes the cross-sectional level of capex intensity and the cross-sectional level of gross profitability — precisely the two published anomaly components the critic identified in the ratio form — leaving only the timing interaction between capacity investment and margin erosion. Because the construct is a difference of two [0,1] own-history ranks, it is scale-, industry- and level-neutral, so it cannot be mechanically absorbed by CMA or RMW, and both tails are populated by real cohorts (expanding commoditizers versus retrenching margin-improvers).
considered.author: proposer

considered.name: ShiftTowardBuyingCapability
considered.hypothesis: A firm that is actively shifting its investment program away from building plant and knowledge internally toward buying capability is making a strategy change that the market prices slowly, and such shifts predict lower returns beyond the standing level of acquisitiveness.
considered.reasoning: This abandons the gross-profit-scaling family entirely and instead isolates one specific design choice within the only mechanism in the archive that produced a reliable FF5 alpha: whether the buy-versus-build effect is a stable firm characteristic (level, tested by the accepted Signal 1) or a transition that arrives as news (change, tested here). Because it is a one-year change in a bounded three-year mix, it is not a function of R&D-reporting status the way the flagged capex-minus-R&D construction was, it retains full coverage through the coalesced acquisition and R&D legs, and a shift in mix leaves total investment scale roughly unchanged so it stays distinct from the level-of-investment sorts CMA neutralizes.
considered.author: proposer

considered.name: KnowledgeVersusPlantInvestmentTiming
considered.hypothesis: Among firms that run research programs, those currently at a five-year high in research intensity while physical investment sits at a five-year low are reallocating toward knowledge capital, and because the research leg is expensed while the retrenched capex leg reads as contraction, the market underreacts.
considered.reasoning: This applies the winning own-history-rank construction to the two investment channels directly, so both legs are [0,1] within-firm percentiles and neither dollar magnitude nor industry membership can dominate — the flaw that broke the earlier difference-in-changes substitution index. Using xrd uncoalesced deliberately restricts the sample to innovators, which removes the R&D-reporting-status contamination the critic identified in the peak-relative and count-based signals, so the sort is a genuine intra-firm reallocation test.
considered.author: proposer

considered.name: InventoryBuildAgainstMarginErosion
considered.hypothesis: Physical stock-building is only warranted when the firm's product differentiation is intact; a firm whose inventory relative to sales is at a five-year high precisely when its gross margin is at a five-year low is pushing goods into a market that is no longer paying for them, and future markdowns follow.
considered.reasoning: This moves the winning timing-contrast construction to the working-capital channel, which was the other flow signal with a real FMB slope (InventoryBuildPerGrossProfit, fmb −3.0), while eliminating the objection that a level ratio of capex to gross profit is a mechanical quotient of two published anomalies — both legs here are own-history ranks, so cross-sectional inventory intensity and cross-sectional gross profitability are differenced out. Testing plant and inventory under identical construction tells us whether the mechanism is capacity-specific or a general physical-overexpansion-into-commoditization effect.
considered.author: proposer

considered.name: InvestmentMixInstability
considered.hypothesis: A firm that keeps swinging the split of its investment budget between plant and research lacks a stable strategy or is financially constrained into stop-start project funding, and such instability in intangible commitment destroys the option value of research and predicts low returns.
considered.reasoning: This is a second-moment mechanism entirely absent from the archive: the signal is zero-information about the *level* of either investment channel and only measures the stability of their mix, so it is orthogonal to CMA, to R&D intensity, and to the timing contrasts elsewhere in this batch. Restricting to firms reporting both capex and R&D keeps the ratio well defined and avoids the degenerate zero-volatility mass that coalescing would create for non-innovators.
considered.author: proposer

considered.name: AcquisitionSourcingRankVersusResearchSourcingRank
considered.hypothesis: Firms that have sourced their capability over the past five years mainly by purchasing companies rather than by funding internal research have paid market prices for intangibles, and this cumulative sourcing tilt predicts lower returns than an equally sized internally funded program.
considered.reasoning: The flagged version differenced two at-scaled cumulative intensities with very unequal dispersion, so it degenerated into minus R&D intensity; rank-standardizing each leg before differencing forces the two channels to contribute equally, which is the minimal change that actually identifies the sourcing mix. The two legs are not independent bets but two mutually exclusive ways of buying the same thing — capability — so their rank difference is a composition measure, and it isolates the continuous-intensity design choice against the archived binary year-count version that produced a −5.5% alpha with a flat FMB slope.
considered.author: proposer

considered.name: GoodwillOverhangWithRealInvestmentRetreat
considered.hypothesis: Acquired intangible capital is impaired in economic terms when it stops generating rents; firms whose goodwill is at a five-year high relative to the gross profit it produces, while their physical reinvestment rate is at a five-year low, are harvesting rather than sustaining acquired businesses and face writedowns and disappointment.
considered.reasoning: Scaling goodwill by gross profit rather than by net plant removes the mechanical upward drift the critic identified — goodwill over plant rises automatically because plant depreciates, whereas goodwill over gross profit rises only when acquisitions fail to deliver rents, so the own-history rank is no longer pinned at its maximum with ties. Replacing the margin leg with the firm's own physical reinvestment rank also means the signal is no longer approximately the negative of a profitability-timing rank, so it tests acquired-capital overhang jointly with real-investment retreat rather than re-testing margin deterioration.
considered.author: proposer

considered.name: ResearchPushUnderMarginPressure
considered.hypothesis: When gross margins are compressing, firms that respond by pushing research intensity to a five-year high are adapting and rebuilding intangible advantage, and this response is rewarded, in contrast to firms that respond by pushing physical capacity to a five-year high.
