considered.reasoning: Rescaling the research leg by a three-year average asset base, exactly matching the capex-over-plant scaling of the winning capex version, removes the confound the critic identified: a sales contraction no longer mechanically raises leg one while lowering leg two, so the signal cannot max out purely on deteriorating-revenue firms. With that fix the proposal becomes a true mirror of the archive's best signal, holding construction, window and margin leg fixed and switching only the investment channel, which is the sharpest available test of whether tangible and intangible investment carry opposite implications under identical conditions.
considered.author: proposer

considered.name: LaborProductivityGainWithoutCapitalDeepening
considered.hypothesis: Firms whose revenue per employee is climbing to own-history highs without any corresponding deepening of physical capital per employee are generating output from intangible sources — process knowledge, brand, software, organizational capital — and this unrecorded capital formation is underpriced.
considered.reasoning: This introduces the labor channel, which the archive has never successfully used, and frames intangible capital formation as productivity that appears without capital deepening rather than as reported R&D, so it is defined for non-R&D-reporting firms and escapes the reporting-status contamination that has weakened several earlier signals. Both legs are own-history ranks on the same employee base, so the signal is scale-, industry- and level-neutral by construction.
considered.author: proposer

considered.name: JointCapacityAndInventoryOvercommitment
considered.expression: SUB(MIN(TS_RANK(RATIO(capx, MA(ppent, 3)), 5), TS_RANK(RATIO(invt, MA(sale, 3)), 5)), TS_RANK(RATIO(SUB(sale, cogs), sale), 5))
considered.hypothesis: Physical over-commitment is only decisive when it happens in both channels at once: a firm simultaneously at own-history highs in fixed-capacity reinvestment and in inventory relative to sales, while its gross margin sits at an own-history low, is expanding a business whose intangible pricing power is disappearing.
considered.reasoning: Replacing the additive stack with MIN of the two physical legs implements the conjunction the hypothesis actually states — the signal is high only if capacity *and* inventory commitment are both elevated — and the margin leg now enters exactly once, so the construction is no longer dominated by own-history margin reversal. This is a functional-form change rather than a recombination: firms high on only one physical channel are pulled down to their weaker leg instead of being averaged into the top bucket.
considered.author: proposer

considered.name: ResearchPivotDuringMarginCompression
considered.expression: MIN(TS_RANK(RATIO(xrd, ADD(capx, xrd)), 5), TS_RANK(NEG(RATIO(SUB(sale, cogs), sale)), 5))
considered.hypothesis: Innovators that pivot their investment budget toward research at the moment their margins are most compressed are adapting to competitive erosion by rebuilding intangible advantage, and this conjunction of pressure and reallocation is rewarded.
considered.reasoning: Using MIN instead of a rank difference removes the sign contradiction the critic identified: the margin leg no longer enters additively with the same coefficient it carries in the negatively signed capacity signal, and the signal only fires when both conditions hold, which is the conditional mechanism the hypothesis describes. The R&D-reporter restriction is deliberate rather than incidental — the hypothesis is about how an existing research program is redirected — and the archive shows this subsample can still deliver a strong cross-sectional slope (KnowledgeVersusPlantInvestmentTiming, fmb 3.85 at 0.06 coverage).
considered.author: proposer

considered.name: SlowMovingCapacityOvercommitment
considered.hypothesis: Over-commitment to physical capacity in the face of eroding product-market rents is a multi-year state rather than a single-year coincidence: firms whose three-year cumulative capacity spending is at an own-history high while their three-year average gross margin is at an own-history low are the ones that will disappoint.
considered.reasoning: This abandons the cumulative capex-versus-R&D stack the critic rejected as two published anomalies added together, and instead isolates a specific design choice on the archive's best signal — measurement horizon — by smoothing both legs to three years while keeping the own-history-rank machinery. If the horizon-smoothed version strengthens the alpha and Sharpe, the mechanism is persistent strategic over-commitment; if it weakens, the effect is genuinely a one-year timing coincidence, and either outcome sharpens the remaining generations at full coverage.
considered.author: proposer

considered.name: CapacityAdditionAgainstRentYieldOnPlant
considered.hypothesis: Capacity additions destroy value when each existing unit of plant is generating unusually little gross profit: the rent yield on physical capacity, which is determined by intangible advantages such as brand, product design and process knowledge, tells the firm whether more plant is worth building.
considered.reasoning: This repairs both flagged defects: the second leg is now gross profit per unit of plant, an explicitly intangible-rent measure built from sale and cogs, so the signal is genuinely cross-theme, and the investment leg is scaled by average assets rather than by plant, so heavy capex no longer mechanically raises one leg while depressing the other. It is distinct from the archived margin-timing signal because it conditions on the *level of rents earned per unit of capacity* rather than on the margin rate, separating rent scarcity from price erosion.
considered.author: proposer

considered.name: PivotFromBoughtToBuiltAfterWritedown
considered.hypothesis: Firms that have just shrunk their goodwill — through impairment or divestiture of acquired businesses — while simultaneously ramping organic investment in plant and research to own-history highs are pivoting from buying capability to building it, and the market underreacts to this strategic reversal because the writedown dominates reported earnings.
considered.reasoning: This is not a re-signing of the goodwill-overhang construction: the acquired-capital leg is now the *change* in goodwill (a realized writedown or disposal event) rather than its level relative to gross profit, and the investment leg is an organic-investment *ramp* rather than a retreat, so the identified cohort is the opposite one. The MIN form requires both conditions jointly, giving a clean post-impairment reallocation cohort whose positive expected sign follows from earnings-based underreaction rather than from the earlier weak contrary result.
considered.author: proposer

considered.name: BrandPushVersusCapacityPush
considered.hypothesis: Among firms that advertise, those currently pushing brand investment to an own-history high while physical capacity spending sits at an own-history low are building customer-based intangible capital instead of replicable plant, and this reallocation is underpriced because advertising is fully expensed.
considered.reasoning: Advertising is the one intangible channel in the resource menu the archive has never tested on its own, and the brand-versus-plant contrast is economically distinct from the research-versus-plant contrast because brand capital depreciates faster and pays off in demand rather than in product capability. The construction reuses the validated own-history-rank machinery so the result is interpretable against the existing family, and any positive finding would extend the theme's central claim beyond R&D.
considered.author: proposer

considered.name: RentPerWorkerVersusCapitalPerWorker
considered.hypothesis: Firms whose gross profit per employee is climbing to own-history highs without any deepening of plant per employee are earning rents from organizational and knowledge capital that never appears on the balance sheet, and this unrecorded capital formation is underpriced.
considered.reasoning: The accepted labor signal produced a strong cross-sectional slope (fmb 3.57) but no alpha, which is the signature of a revenue-scale confound; replacing revenue per worker with *gross profit* per worker isolates rent generation rather than sales volume, and gross profitability is the margin concept that has driven every successful signal in this archive. This is a single, targeted scaling change that identifies whether the labor channel's information is about intangible rents or merely about growth.
considered.author: proposer

considered.name: TotalPhysicalCommitmentAgainstMarginErosion
considered.expression: SUB(TS_RANK(RATIO(ADD(capx, DELTA(invt, 1)), MA(at, 3)), 5), TS_RANK(RATIO(SUB(sale, cogs), sale), 5))
considered.hypothesis: The economically relevant quantity is total dollars committed to physical assets — new plant plus incremental inventory — relative to the firm's size, and committing an own-history-high share of assets to hard assets while gross margin is at an own-history low predicts low returns.
considered.reasoning: The archive contains a rank-conjunction of the capacity and inventory channels (MIN form, alpha −2.3%) but never their economically natural dollar sum, which weights each channel by how much capital it actually absorbs rather than by percentile position and avoids the double-counted margin leg the critic rejected. Scaling by average assets rather than by plant also breaks the shared-denominator artifact present in the capex-over-plant leg, so this is a substantive measurement improvement rather than a recombination.
considered.author: proposer

considered.name: AcquisitiveNonInnovatorsOvercommittingNow
considered.expression: MIN(RANK(SUB(TS_RANK(RATIO(capx, MA(ppent, 3)), 5), TS_RANK(RATIO(SUB(sale, cogs), sale), 5))), MIN(RANK(TS_SUM(RATIO(COALESCE(aqc, 0), at), 5)), RANK(NEG(TS_SUM(RATIO(COALESCE(xrd, 0), at), 5)))))
considered.hypothesis: The worst-positioned firms satisfy three conditions at once — they have bought capability rather than built it over five years, they have no research base, and they are right now pushing physical capacity while their gross margin sits at an own-history low.
considered.reasoning: Replacing the additive SUMRANK with a nested MIN over three cross-sectionally ranked legs implements the conjunction the hypothesis states: a firm scores high only if it is simultaneously acquisitive, research-poor and currently over-committing, so the top bucket is a genuinely intersected cohort rather than an average of two validated sorts. Putting all three legs on the same [0,1] cross-sectional rank scale also fixes the scale-mixing problem, and coverage remains near 0.12 because every leg is defined for non-R&D reporters.
considered.author: proposer

considered.name: OvercommitmentWhereKnowledgeEndowmentIsAbsent
considered.expression: MIN(RANK(SUB(TS_RANK(RATIO(capx, MA(ppent, 3)), 5), TS_RANK(RATIO(SUB(sale, cogs), sale), 5))), IND_RANK(NEG(RATIO(COALESCE(xrd, 0), MA(sale, 3)))))
considered.hypothesis: Pushing capacity into eroding margins is punished mainly when the firm has no knowledge endowment relative to its own industry peers, because a research base offers an alternative route back to rents while a purely hard-asset firm can only compete on price.
considered.reasoning: The MIN form makes the knowledge-endowment leg a genuine gate rather than an additive term, so the signal fires only for firms that are simultaneously over-committing and research-poor, which is what the hypothesis claims. Using IND_RANK rather than a plain cross-sectional rank strips out the sector-level component that constitutes the published R&D-intensity anomaly, leaving within-industry knowledge poverty as the conditioning variable, and it puts the gate on the same [0,1] scale as the ranked timing contrast.
considered.author: proposer

considered.name: OvercommitmentFundedFromOutsideCapital
considered.expression: MIN(RANK(SUB(TS_RANK(RATIO(capx, MA(ppent, 3)), 5), TS_RANK(RATIO(SUB(sale, cogs), sale), 5))), RANK(WINSOR(RATIO(ADD(sstk, DELTA(dltt, 1)), ADD(capx, COALESCE(xrd, 0))), 1)))
considered.hypothesis: Capacity expansion into eroding margins is destructive specifically when the money comes from outside investors rather than from the firm's own cash generation, because external funding severs the discipline that a shrinking rent base would otherwise impose on the investment decision.
considered.reasoning: Two changes address the critique: the financing leg is now a *funding-mix ratio* — outside capital raised per dollar of total investment spending, including the knowledge-investment channel — rather than an issuance level, so it is not the net-external-financing anomaly in disguise, and the legs are combined with MIN so the signal fires only under the joint condition the hypothesis specifies. Both legs are cross-sectional ranks in [0,1], and winsorizing the funding ratio controls the small-denominator tail for firms with negligible investment.
considered.author: proposer

considered.name: KnowledgeRichCapitalRestraintWithMarginRepair
considered.expression: MUL(RANK(SUB(TS_RANK(RATIO(SUB(sale, cogs), sale), 5), TS_RANK(RATIO(capx, MA(ppent, 3)), 5))), IND_RANK(RATIO(COALESCE(xrd, 0), MA(sale, 3))))
considered.hypothesis: The long side of the theme is the mirror image of the short side: firms whose gross margins are at own-history highs while physical capital commitment is at own-history lows, and which carry a strong research base relative to peers, are compounding intangible advantage without absorbing capital, and this is underpriced.
considered.reasoning: Every strong result in this archive is on the short side, and the positive-signed candidates (PeakRelative at t 1.78, KnowledgeVersusPlantTiming with no alpha) were never given the gating structure that made the short side work, so this tests whether the conjunction mechanism is symmetric or whether the effect is purely a distress/over-commitment phenomenon. It keeps full coverage through the zero-R&D convention and the industry-relative endowment gate, so a positive result would not be a repackaged R&D-intensity sort.
considered.author: proposer

considered.name: CapacityPushIntoDeterioratingRentTrend
considered.hypothesis: What matters for capacity decisions is the direction in which the firm's intangible pricing power is moving, not merely where the current margin sits in its own history: committing capital while the five-year margin trend is steeply negative signals expansion into structural competitive decline.
considered.reasoning: Every successful signal in the archive uses the *position* of the margin in its own five-year history, which conflates cyclical dips with structural erosion; substituting a five-year fitted margin trend tests whether the mechanism is about direction of decline, and if so this variant should improve both the slope and the alpha because it removes mean-reverting margin noise from the gate. The capex leg stays as an own-history rank so no cross-sectional investment level enters, keeping the construct outside CMA's span.
considered.author: proposer

considered.name: NetHardAssetCommitmentAgainstMarginErosion
considered.expression: SUB(TS_RANK(RATIO(SUB(capx, COALESCE(xrd, 0)), MA(at, 3)), 5), TS_RANK(RATIO(SUB(sale, cogs), sale), 5))
considered.hypothesis: What is punished is hard-asset accumulation *net of* knowledge accumulation: a firm putting an own-history-high share of its asset base into plant beyond what it spends on research, precisely while gross margin sits at an own-history low, is deepening a commoditizing business instead of renewing its advantage.
considered.reasoning: Rather than smoothing an existing gate, this moves the intangible channel inside the commitment measure itself: the investment leg is now a signed tangible-minus-knowledge spending balance, so the same firm is scored differently depending on whether its capex is accompanied by research, which is the theme's mechanism expressed continuously rather than as an extreme-cohort intersection. It keeps full coverage through the zero-R&D convention, scales by average assets so the two channels are commensurable, and remains a within-firm timing contrast that no cross-sectional investment factor spans.
considered.author: proposer

considered.name: LeveragingUpWhileStarvingIntangibles
considered.expression: SUB(TS_RANK(RATIO(DELTA(ADD(dltt, dlc), 1), MA(at, 3)), 5), TS_RANK(RATIO(ADD(COALESCE(xrd, 0), COALESCE(xad, 0)), MA(sale, 3)), 5))
considered.hypothesis: Firms adding debt at an own-history-high rate while cutting research and brand spending to own-history lows are financing current obligations by mortgaging their intangible future, and this substitution of leverage for intangible investment predicts low returns.
considered.reasoning: This abandons the funding-gate construction entirely and pairs the financing channel directly against the intangible-spending channel, both as own-history ranks, so it tests a distinct economic mechanism — debt-for-intangibles substitution — rather than re-aggregating the archived capacity-timing legs. Coverage stays full because both intangible spending items are coalesced to zero under the standard non-reporting convention, and because neither leg is a cross-sectional level the construct is not the leverage or issuance anomaly.
considered.author: proposer

considered.name: InnovatorPivotingToAcquiredCapability
considered.hypothesis: Among firms that actually run research programs, those whose acquisition spending has climbed to an own-history high while their research intensity has fallen to an own-history low are substituting purchased capability for internal capability, and this within-firm pivot predicts low returns.
considered.reasoning: The archive's buy-versus-build evidence is entirely cross-sectional, which is precisely why it yields large alphas with no cross-sectional slope — the level of acquisitiveness is a sticky firm characteristic. Recasting buy-versus-build as a *within-firm timing* contrast on the same asset scale, in the subsample where both channels are genuinely available, tests whether the pivot itself carries information, and it avoids the extreme-cohort concentration problem the critic identified in stacked rank products.
considered.author: proposer

considered.name: TotalCapitalAbsorptionAgainstRentMomentum
considered.expression: SUB(TS_RANK(RATIO(ADD(ADD(capx, COALESCE(xrd, 0)), DELTA(invt, 1)), MA(at, 3)), 5), TS_RANK(GROWTH(SUB(sale, cogs), 1), 5))
considered.hypothesis: If the over-commitment effect is specific to tangible investment, then a commitment measure that also counts knowledge spending should predict returns more weakly: total capital absorption at an own-history high while gross-profit growth is at an own-history low should be a materially softer negative signal than its tangible-only counterpart.
considered.reasoning: This replaces the rejected gross-profitability placebo gate with a cleaner adjudication of the theme's central claim: the intangible channel enters by being *added into* the commitment measure rather than by gating it, and the rent leg is switched from margin level to gross-profit growth so the margin term is not double-counted. Comparing its strength against the tangible-only signals tells us directly whether the archive's alphas come from tangible over-commitment or from capital absorption generally, which is decisive information for the final generations.
considered.author: proposer

considered.name: CapitalRestraintGatedByKnowledgeStockShare
considered.expression: MUL(RANK(SUB(TS_RANK(RATIO(SUB(sale, cogs), sale), 5), TS_RANK(RATIO(capx, MA(ppent, 3)), 5))), IND_RANK(RATIO(TS_SUM(COALESCE(xrd, 0), 3), ADD(ppent, TS_SUM(COALESCE(xrd, 0), 3)))))
considered.hypothesis: The long-side effect operates through the composition of the firm's accumulated capital — knowledge stock relative to physical stock — rather than through the level of its current research spending: capital-light firms repairing margins pay off most when their capital base is already knowledge-weighted.
considered.reasoning: The archive's best positive signal gated on industry-relative R&D-to-sales, which the critic correctly noted cannot be separated from the published R&D-intensity anomaly; replacing that gate with an industry-relative *capital-composition* measure tests the same economic claim with a variable that is a stock mix rather than a spending intensity. If the joint evidence survives the substitution, the mechanism is genuinely about intangible capital composition, which is exactly the theme's claim and the most valuable thing to establish before the final generations.
considered.author: proposer

considered.name: SignedRestraintInteractionWithKnowledgeEndowment
considered.expression: MUL(SUB(TS_RANK(RATIO(SUB(sale, cogs), sale), 5), TS_RANK(RATIO(capx, MA(ppent, 3)), 5)), IND_RANK(RATIO(COALESCE(xrd, 0), MA(sale, 3))))
considered.hypothesis: Knowledge endowment amplifies the return consequences of capital-allocation timing in both directions: among research-rich firms, capital restraint with margin repair is strongly rewarded and capacity pushing into margin erosion is strongly punished, while research-poor firms show a muted response either way.
considered.reasoning: The archive's best positive signal ranked the contrast before gating, which discards its sign and forces knowledge-poor firms to the bottom of the sort; keeping the contrast signed in [−1, 1] and multiplying by a [0, 1] endowment weight makes the construct a genuine interaction slope, with knowledge-poor firms pooled near zero in the middle and both extremes occupied by knowledge-rich firms on opposite sides of the allocation decision. This is a structural change rather than an aggregator swap, and it directly tests whether the effect is a one-sided cohort or a true amplification.
considered.author: proposer

considered.name: MaturedResearchPayoffWithCapitalRestraint
considered.expression: MUL(RANK(SUB(TS_RANK(RATIO(SUB(sale, cogs), MA(at, 3)), 5), TS_RANK(RATIO(capx, MA(ppent, 3)), 5))), IND_RANK(RATIO(COALESCE(LAG(xrd, 3), 0), MA(sale, 3))))
considered.hypothesis: Research pays off with a multi-year lag: firms whose gross profit per unit of assets is now at an own-history high while capital spending stays at an own-history low, and which were heavy researchers three years ago, are harvesting matured intangible investment that the market never capitalized.
considered.reasoning: Every intangible leg in the archive is contemporaneous, which conflates spending with payoff; lagging the endowment gate three years imposes the actual economics of the research-to-rent conversion and makes the long leg a harvest cohort rather than a high-spending cohort. The rent leg is also switched from margin rate to gross profit per unit of assets so the signal captures rent *scale* generated on a capital base that is not growing, and the zero convention on unreported past research keeps coverage at full sample width.
considered.author: proposer

considered.name: AcceleratingNetHardAssetCommitment
considered.expression: SUB(TS_RANK(ACCEL(RATIO(SUB(capx, COALESCE(xrd, 0)), MA(at, 3))), 5), TS_RANK(RATIO(SUB(sale, cogs), sale), 5))
considered.hypothesis: Over-commitment is most damaging when it is still accelerating: a firm whose net hard-asset commitment rate is rising at an own-history-high pace while gross margin sits at an own-history low is escalating a losing capital-allocation decision rather than merely maintaining a high level.
considered.reasoning: Rather than uniting two archived commitment legs, this changes the temporal content of the leg from level-in-own-history to change-in-change, which distinguishes chronic capital-heavy firms (already captured by the archive) from firms actively escalating hard-asset spending net of research — a different economic state with a different expected persistence. The rent leg and window are held fixed so the comparison against the archived level version is clean, and coverage stays at full sample width through the standard zero-research convention.
considered.author: proposer

considered.name: SignedNetCommitmentAmplifiedByKnowledgePoverty
considered.expression: MUL(SUB(TS_RANK(RATIO(SUB(capx, COALESCE(xrd, 0)), MA(at, 3)), 5), TS_RANK(RATIO(SUB(sale, cogs), sale), 5)), IND_RANK(NEG(RATIO(COALESCE(xrd, 0), MA(sale, 3)))))
considered.hypothesis: Knowledge poverty amplifies the penalty for net hard-asset over-commitment in both directions: among firms with no research base relative to peers, committing capital while margins erode is severely punished and restraint while margins repair is rewarded, whereas research-rich firms respond weakly either way.
considered.reasoning: This is the short-side counterpart to the accepted signed long-side interaction, and it differs structurally from every gated signal in the archive: the contrast keeps its sign in [−1, 1] instead of being pre-ranked, and the commitment leg is the netted capex-minus-research measure that preserved the cross-sectional slope where hard MIN gates destroyed it. Knowledge-rich firms are pooled near zero in the middle rather than pushed to one tail, so the sort's extremes are opposite allocation decisions by the same type of firm — a genuine amplification test rather than a cohort intersection.
considered.author: proposer

considered.name: TangibilityDriftAgainstPeersWithMarginErosion
considered.hypothesis: Firms whose asset base is drifting toward hard capital relative to their industry peers, at the same time as their own gross margin falls to an own-history low, are losing the intangible race in their product market and will underperform.
considered.reasoning: The degenerate leg is removed: industry-relative tangibility is defined for every firm from ppent and at, so no part of the sample is sorted on an industry research trend the way an industry-adjusted coalesced R&D leg would be. Economically it shifts the intangible dimension from own spending to competitive capital-structure position — the firm becoming more hard-asset-dependent than its peers while its own rents erode — which is a channel the archive has not tested and which stays a within-firm timing contrast, keeping it outside CMA and RMW.
considered.author: proposer

considered.name: MaturedKnowledgeStockHarvest
considered.expression: MUL(RANK(SUB(TS_RANK(RATIO(SUB(sale, cogs), MA(at, 3)), 5), TS_RANK(RATIO(capx, MA(ppent, 3)), 5))), IND_RANK(RATIO(TS_SUM(COALESCE(LAG(xrd, 2), 0), 3), MA(sale, 3))))
considered.hypothesis: What is harvested is a *stock* of matured research, not a single vintage: firms with high cumulative research spending from three to five years ago that are now producing rising gross profit on a static capital base are monetizing an unrecorded knowledge stock the market never capitalized.
considered.reasoning: If the winner's three-year lag captured a genuine conversion delay, replacing the single lagged year with the cumulative research of the three years ending three years ago should be strictly less noisy and therefore strengthen both the slope and the alpha; if it does not, the lag was picking up mean reversion in a single noisy observation. The gate stays industry-relative so sector R&D norms are removed, and coverage is unchanged at roughly 0.12 through the standard zero-research convention.
considered.author: proposer

considered.name: SignedRestraintWithMaturedResearchGate
considered.expression: MUL(SUB(TS_RANK(RATIO(SUB(sale, cogs), MA(at, 3)), 5), TS_RANK(RATIO(capx, MA(ppent, 3)), 5)), IND_RANK(RATIO(COALESCE(LAG(xrd, 3), 0), MA(sale, 3))))
considered.hypothesis: Past research endowment amplifies the return consequences of current capital allocation in both directions: among firms that were heavy researchers three years ago, rent expansion with capital restraint is strongly rewarded and rent contraction with capacity pushing is strongly punished, while firms with no research history respond weakly either way.
considered.reasoning: This combines the two independently best-performing design features in the archive — the signed contrast, which delivered the strongest cross-sectional slope (fmb +4.79), and the lagged research gate, which delivered the strongest alpha and Sharpe (+3.9%, 0.47) — into one construction, and it is a structural change rather than a recombination because keeping the sign places knowledge-poor firms in the middle instead of the bottom tail. It is the most likely candidate to carry both forms of evidence into the final generation.
considered.author: proposer

considered.name: ResearchCommitmentPersistenceHarvest
considered.expression: MUL(RANK(SUB(TS_RANK(RATIO(SUB(sale, cogs), MA(at, 3)), 5), TS_RANK(RATIO(capx, MA(ppent, 3)), 5))), IND_RANK(TS_SUM(INDICATOR(RATIO(COALESCE(xrd, 0), sale), 0.02), 5)))
considered.hypothesis: What creates a harvestable unrecorded knowledge stock is sustained commitment rather than the level of any single year's spending: firms that maintained material research in most of the past five years and are now producing own-history-high gross profit on a static capital base are monetizing accumulated capability the balance sheet never recorded.
considered.reasoning: The gate is a new economic construct for this frame — a five-year frequency of material research commitment, industry-ranked — rather than a re-timed version of research intensity, and the archive's evidence that persistence counts carried large alphas (AcquirerYearsMinusInnovatorYears) supports its relevance. It also removes a weakness of intensity gates: a single spike in R&D-to-sales caused by collapsing sales cannot qualify a firm as research-rich, which should sharpen both the slope and the portfolio composition.
considered.author: proposer

considered.name: RentYieldOnTotalCapitalIncludingKnowledge
considered.expression: SUB(TS_RANK(RATIO(SUB(sale, cogs), ADD(MA(ppent, 3), TS_SUM(COALESCE(LAG(xrd, 2), 0), 3))), 5), TS_RANK(RATIO(capx, MA(ppent, 3)), 5))
considered.hypothesis: The economically correct denominator for rent generation is physical capital plus the matured knowledge stock that produced those rents; firms whose return on this total capital base is at an own-history high while physical investment is at an own-history low are compounding intangible advantage without absorbing capital.
considered.reasoning: This is not an ablation of the winner but a new measurement idea: the intangible channel enters the *denominator of a rent yield* rather than as an external gate, so knowledge capital is treated as capital rather than as a firm characteristic, and the signal is defined for every firm through the standard zero-research convention. Using research lagged two to four years matches the conversion delay that the archive's lagged gate identified, and both legs stay own-history ranks so no cross-sectional profitability or investment level enters.
considered.author: proposer

considered.name: ResearchAbandonmentWhilePushingCapacity
considered.expression: MUL(SUB(TS_RANK(RATIO(capx, MA(ppent, 3)), 5), TS_RANK(RATIO(COALESCE(xrd, 0), MA(at, 3)), 5)), IND_RANK(RATIO(COALESCE(LAG(xrd, 3), 0), MA(sale, 3))))
considered.hypothesis: Former heavy researchers that have cut research to own-history lows while pushing plant spending to own-history highs are abandoning an intangible strategy in favour of replicable capacity, and this reversal of strategic direction predicts low returns.
considered.reasoning: This is a distinct economic state from the knowledge-poverty interaction already in the archive: the gate selects firms that *had* a research base three years ago, and the contrast then identifies those now dismantling it, so the short leg is pipeline abandonment rather than chronic hard-asset dependence. Because the gate and the current-research leg use different vintages of the same variable, the signal cannot be reproduced by a combination of the archived signed contrast and its knowledge-poverty version.
considered.author: proposer

considered.name: BuiltShareOfIntangibleBaseHarvest
considered.expression: MUL(RANK(SUB(TS_RANK(RATIO(SUB(sale, cogs), MA(at, 3)), 5), TS_RANK(RATIO(capx, MA(ppent, 3)), 5))), IND_RANK(RATIO(TS_SUM(COALESCE(xrd, 0), 3), ADD(TS_SUM(COALESCE(xrd, 0), 3), COALESCE(intan, 0)))))
considered.hypothesis: The harvest premium accrues specifically to firms whose intangible base was internally built and therefore never capitalized: among capital-light firms with rising rents, those whose knowledge capital comes from their own research rather than from acquired intangibles are the ones the market misprices.
considered.reasoning: The double-count is removed — the gate now contrasts cumulative research against reported intangible assets, which already subsume goodwill, so it measures the *built share* of the intangible base rather than adding goodwill twice. The prediction is a genuine positive one rather than a placebo: if unrecorded capital is the source of the mispricing, the built-share gate should be at least as strong as the raw research-intensity gate, and it delivers the built-versus-bought adjudication with an alpha-seeking sign.
considered.author: proposer

considered.name: NetCommitmentRestraintInResearchFranchises
considered.expression: MUL(SUB(TS_RANK(RATIO(SUB(sale, cogs), MA(at, 3)), 5), TS_RANK(RATIO(SUB(capx, COALESCE(xrd, 0)), MA(at, 3)), 5)), IND_RANK(TS_SUM(INDICATOR(RATIO(COALESCE(xrd, 0), sale), 0.02), 5)))
considered.hypothesis: Restraint should be measured on hard assets net of knowledge spending, so that a research franchise is not scored as profligate merely for funding research: firms whose rents are at own-history highs while net hard-asset commitment is at own-history lows, and which persistently invest in research, are the purest harvest cohort.
considered.reasoning: This unifies the best-validated commitment measure on the short side (capex net of research over assets, fmb −4.79, Sharpe −0.33) with the best-validated gate on the long side, correcting a real inconsistency in the current winners, whose capex-over-plant leg penalizes exactly the research-intensive firms the gate selects. Keeping the contrast signed places non-franchise firms in the middle of the sort rather than in the short tail, which is the structure that produced the archive's strongest cross-sectional slopes.
considered.author: proposer

considered.name: ScalableRentPerWorkerInResearchFranchises
considered.expression: MUL(RANK(SUB(TS_RANK(RATIO(SUB(sale, cogs), emp), 5), TS_RANK(RATIO(ppent, emp), 5))), IND_RANK(TS_SUM(INDICATOR(RATIO(COALESCE(xrd, 0), sale), 0.02), 5)))
considered.hypothesis: Rising gross profit per employee without capital deepening signals intangible-driven scalability, but it is only mispriced when the underlying capability is internally built and unrecorded; among persistent researchers this labour-productivity gain is a genuine unrecorded-capital signal rather than a cyclical revenue effect.
considered.reasoning: The labour channel has repeatedly produced strong cross-sectional slopes with no portfolio alpha (fmb +3.19 to +3.57, t-alpha ≈ 0.05–0.46), the signature of a signal whose extreme deciles are populated by the wrong firms; adding the research-franchise gate is the specific economic fix, since it restricts the long leg to firms whose productivity gains plausibly come from unrecorded knowledge capital. This is the one remaining untested combination that could add an economically distinct input channel — labour rather than capital — to the winning mechanism.
considered.author: proposer

considered.name: FranchiseDismantlingWhilePushingPlant
considered.hypothesis: The mirror of the harvest is dismantling: firms that built a persistent research franchise in earlier years but have now cut research to own-history lows while pushing plant spending to own-history highs are liquidating intangible capability in favour of replicable capacity, and this reversal predicts low returns.
considered.reasoning: The archived abandonment signal used a single lagged research vintage as the gate and delivered the archive's strongest short-side slope (fmb −4.86) with a modest alpha (−2.1%); replacing that gate with franchise *persistence* targets firms with a genuine multi-year research history to dismantle, which should concentrate the short leg on real strategic reversals rather than on one-off spending dips. It also completes the symmetry test of the winning mechanism using the gate construct that proved strongest on the long side.
considered.author: proposer

considered.name: TotalPhysicalRestraintHarvest
considered.expression: MUL(RANK(SUB(TS_RANK(RATIO(SUB(sale, cogs), MA(at, 3)), 5), TS_RANK(RATIO(ADD(capx, DELTA(invt, 1)), MA(at, 3)), 5))), IND_RANK(TS_SUM(INDICATOR(RATIO(COALESCE(xrd, 0), sale), 0.02), 5)))
considered.hypothesis: Genuine capital restraint means withholding dollars from every hard-asset channel, plant and working capital alike; research franchises whose rents rise while total physical commitment falls to own-history lows are the cleanest case of intangible capital doing the work.
considered.reasoning: The dollar-summed physical commitment measure was validated independently on the short side (fmb −4.71, alpha −2.3%) and captures firms that restrain plant while quietly building inventory, which the capex-over-plant leg misses entirely, so this is a measurement upgrade to the restraint leg rather than a re-aggregation of ranks. Combined with the persistence gate that produced the archive's best Sharpe, it is the most complete version of the mechanism this search has identified and a suitable final candidate.
considered.author: proposer

considered.name: RisingResearchFranchiseHarvest
considered.expression: MUL(RANK(SUB(TS_RANK(RATIO(SUB(sale, cogs), MA(at, 3)), 5), TS_RANK(RATIO(capx, MA(ppent, 3)), 5))), IND_RANK(TREND(RATIO(COALESCE(xrd, 0), MA(sale, 3)), 5)))
considered.hypothesis: The harvest premium is largest where the knowledge pipeline is still being expanded: firms whose research intensity has been on a rising five-year trend relative to peers, and which are now producing own-history-high rents on a static capital base, are monetizing matured research while continuing to build the next vintage, so the mispricing does not self-correct.
considered.reasoning: The gate content is genuinely different from every archived version — a fitted five-year *trend* in research intensity measures the direction of intangible commitment rather than its level, its persistence count, or a lagged vintage, and it distinguishes an expanding franchise from a mature one harvesting a declining pipeline. Industry-ranking the trend removes sector-wide shifts in research norms, non-reporters sit in the middle of the gate rather than at an artificial extreme, and coverage stays near the 0.12 full-sample width of the winning family.
considered.author: proposer

considered.name: FranchiseCashBuildWithCapitalRestraint
considered.hypothesis: Genuine intangible capital shows up as cash: persistent researchers whose cash balances are climbing to own-history highs while plant spending sits at own-history lows are converting unrecorded knowledge capital into liquidity rather than absorbing capital, and the market underprices this because the underlying asset never appears on the balance sheet.
considered.reasoning: This replaces the sign-flipped reallocation contrast with an entirely new outcome variable for the harvest mechanism — internal liquidity accumulation, using the one investment-menu variable (che) that this search has never employed — so it is neither a rediscovery of the abandonment signal nor the negative of any other proposal in this batch. It also tests the mechanism's economic content more directly than a rent-margin leg: if research franchises with capital restraint are truly harvesting, the cash must accumulate, and the gate ensures the long leg is built from committed innovators rather than cash-rich firms generally.
considered.author: proposer

critic_notes.rationale: Internally consistent and correctly signed, but it is essentially an equal-weight blend of two well-documented anomalies (capex/asset growth and R&D intensity) rather than a genuine interaction, since SUMRANK cannot distinguish "hard-asset growth without intangible backing" from a firm that is merely high on one leg.

This is close to a direct rediscovery of the acquisition/external-growth component of the asset-growth anomaly (aqc/lagged assets), and adding DELTA(gdwl) double-counts the same transactions rather than adding an intangible-specific dimension.

Well-constructed and coherent, but intangible-adjusted (Peters–Taylor style) capital growth is already published and will be very highly correlated with plain asset growth, making this a refinement of a known anomaly rather than a cross-theme discovery.

The indicator logic correctly switches on for sub-2% R&D-to-sales firms and the negative sign matches the expression, but zeroing out R&D-intensive firms plants them in the middle of the cross-section as a large mass point, which will dilute and destabilize the sorted spread relative to a proper subsample test.

A genuinely novel, economically coherent composition-of-investment state variable whose positive sign matches the expression; the main risk is the large mass point at exactly zero from non-R&D firms and an unstable denominator when capx+xrd is near zero.

Beyond being a blend of the known net-external-financing and R&D-intensity anomalies, it is internally inconsistent: xrd is not coalesced, so firms with no reported R&D program—the exact "cheap capital, no innovation" cohort the hypothesis targets—are dropped from coverage.

This is a cosmetic re-specification of the archived TangibilityWeightedCapacityGrowth — identical two-leg multiplicative structure with only industry z-scoring, winsorization, and a shorter intangible window changed — so it cannot diagnose why that signal's FMB slope and FF5 alpha disagreed.

R&D stock over R&D-plus-plant is a monotone re-scaling of well-documented R&D-intensity/intangible-capital anomalies and is dominated by industry membership, with a large mass point at zero for the roughly half of firms reporting no R&D, so the sort is mostly a sector bet rather than a new cross-theme mechanism.

The buy-versus-build sourcing mix is an economically coherent and genuinely distinct composition variable rather than a rescaled acquisition-intensity anomaly, though it will be undefined when both legs are zero and will pile up at the 0 and 1 boundaries, so coverage and decile stability need close inspection.

The construction effectively becomes employment growth restricted to intangible-intensive firms (low-intensity firms collapse toward zero in the middle of the sort), so the long-short leg is the known hiring-growth anomaly inside a subsample and the stated positive expected sign runs against its documented direction without a mechanism strong enough to justify the reversal.

A three-year-averaged, industry-demeaned level of the R&D share of investment is a near-duplicate of the already-tested R&D-share signal (and of published R&D-intensity results), with industry z-scoring the only substantive change — a portfolio-side patch rather than a new economic hypothesis.

Because ΔR&D is an order of magnitude smaller than Δnet PPE for most firms, the numerator's variance is overwhelmingly driven by −Δppent, making this a sign-flipped restatement of the physical-investment/asset-growth anomaly rather than a measure of substitution between investment channels.

A legitimate and mechanically motivated repair of the archived buy-versus-build ratio (broader denominator, smoothing, coalesced aqc), but the stated cure for boundary spikes is self-contradictory — coalescing missing aqc to zero *creates* a large point mass at exactly 0 — and the dropped ABS lets negative/divestiture aqc push the ratio outside [0,1], so it risks being an acquisition-intensity (known acquirer-underperformance) sort with a degenerate short leg.

Persistence-counting is a genuinely different mechanism from current-year mix and the unit-free frequency legs fix the scale-domination problem, but R&D reporting status is extremely sticky so the second term will be near-binary (0 or 5) for most firms, meaning much of the variation is a re-labelled "no-R&D firm" dummy — a well-documented effect — rather than a new acquirer-versus-innovator contrast.

Cross-sectionally capx/(sale−cogs) is approximately (capx/at)÷(gross profit/at), i.e. a mechanical ratio of two canonical published anomalies — the capex/investment anomaly (Titman-Wei-Xie) in the numerator and gross profitability (Novy-Marx) in the denominator — both signed the same way, so a negative slope would be a rediscovery rather than evidence for the stated pricing-power mechanism, and the claim that gross-profit scaling escapes CMA is asserted without argument.

With xrd coalesced to zero, this collapses exactly to Signal 3 for the majority of firms that report no R&D, and for the rest capex typically dominates R&D outside pharma/software, so it is largely a cosmetic variant of the previous proposal whose residual variation is driven by R&D-reporting status rather than the claimed equal-pricing-power tilt; the paired "design test" it promises is therefore not identified.

A coherent stock-based complement to the flow mix that avoids the archived signal's noisy revenue gate, but the numerator is a lifetime cumulative stock while the denominator is only a three-year flow sum, so the ratio mechanically increases with firm age and acquisition history and overlaps substantially with known goodwill-intensity/post-merger underperformance evidence; a large point mass at zero for non-acquirers also weakens the short leg.

Normalizing each channel by its own five-year peak is a genuinely new, scale- and industry-neutral construction that plausibly fixes the undefined spread of the archived substitution index, but the COALESCE(...,0) on the R&D leg assigns all non-R&D firms a value in [−1,0], so the short side is again contaminated by R&D-reporting status, and both legs cluster near 1 for growing firms, likely thinning the extreme buckets.

A defensible reconstruction of the archived PeakRelativeKnowledgeVersusPlantSpending (which was borderline at t 1.78) using the better-behaved own-history-rank machinery rather than peak ratios, though it remains the same reallocation hypothesis and the xrd/MA(sale,3) leg mechanically rises when sales fall, so part of any long-leg return may be a sales-decline/value confound rather than genuine intangible reallocation.

The two legs are differenced in raw, unranked at-scaled units with very unequal dispersion (five-year cumulative xrd/at is far larger and more persistent than aqc/at for the R&D-reporting subsample), so the composite will be dominated by minus R&D intensity — i.e. essentially a restatement of the published R&D-intensity/R&D-to-market anomaly — rather than testing the sourcing-mix mechanism it claims.

A coherent, internally consistent transfer of the archive's best-performing timing-contrast construction to the working-capital channel where an independent FMB slope already existed, with both legs demeaned within firm so it is not simply a repackaging of the known inventory-growth or gross-profitability anomalies, and the sign follows naturally from the expression.

gdwl/(ppent+gdwl) drifts upward almost mechanically because goodwill is not depreciated while net plant is, so its five-year TS_RANK will be pinned near its maximum with heavy ties for most acquirers, collapsing the signal into roughly the negative of a margin-timing rank and thus testing profitability deterioration rather than impairment exposure.

Genuinely a new second-moment mechanism for this pairing and internally consistent, but the volatility of a bounded ratio with lumpy small denominators will load heavily on firm size and general cash-flow/earnings volatility — already-documented return predictors — so the result will need a size and fundamental-volatility control to be interpretable.

The symmetry argument is the right kind of discriminating test, but the construction is not actually the mirror of the winning signal: scaling R&D by MA(sale,3) while the margin leg is also a sales-based ratio means a sales contraction pushes leg one up and leg two down simultaneously, so the signal mechanically maxes out for deteriorating-revenue firms and any positive slope is confounded with value/distress rather than identifying intangible adaptation (scaling xrd by MA(at,3) would fix this).

This is a mechanical sum of two already-archived signals that double-weights the identical gross-margin leg (net signal ≈ capx rank + inventory rank − 2×margin rank), so it is a cosmetic recombination whose dominant driver is own-history margin reversal, and the additive form does not implement the "joint occurrence" conjunction the hypothesis actually describes.

The expression shares the archive's `−TS_RANK(gross margin)` leg but flips the expected sign to positive, so the same component is asserted to predict returns in both directions, and the additive rank difference cannot express the conditional "responds to margin compression by reallocating" mechanism while the xrd-share leg also restricts coverage to R&D reporters (~6% in the analogous archive signal).

This is an additive stack of two well-documented published anomalies — cumulative capex/asset investment (CMA-adjacent) and low R&D intensity — with no genuine interaction, and it is a one-leg substitution into the archive's AcquisitionSourcingRankVersusResearchSourcingRank, so its value is diagnostic rather than as a novel signal.

Economically coherent and cleanly constructed, but it contains no intangible leg at all (so it is not cross-theme) and the two legs share the ppent denominator such that heavy capex mechanically raises leg one and depresses leg two, making the "interaction" partly an accounting artifact rather than an economic conjunction, on top of overlapping with the known asset-turnover/investment-with-low-profitability effects.

Genuinely new channel for this archive, internally consistent (high own-history revenue per worker with no capital deepening → positive), and defined for non-R&D reporters, though it should be checked against the sales-growth anomaly and for emp reporting staleness/rounding noise given the shared employee denominator.

This is the archive's GoodwillOverhangWithRealInvestmentRetreat with a cosmetically broadened numerator and its sign reversed after seeing a weak (t≈1.8) contrary result, i.e. post-hoc sign fitting on a near-duplicate construction rather than a substantively different mechanism, and the resulting story largely restates the known intangible-adjusted value effect.

This is essentially a linear ensemble of two already-evaluated archive signals, and the hypothesis asserts a conjunction ("both structurally tilted... and currently over-committing") that an additive SUMRANK cannot express — any improvement in ls_talpha would come mechanically from averaging two noisy validated sorts rather than from the claimed interaction.

The added leg is a cross-sectional R&D-to-sales rank, i.e. the long-published R&D-intensity anomaly (Chan-Lakonishok-Sougiannis) entering additively, so a negative slope would be at least partly a rediscovery; the stated conditional mechanism ("most damaging for firms with no knowledge endowment") again is not what an additive difference computes, and mixing a coarse 5-point TS_RANK with a continuous cross-sectional RANK undermines the claimed scale comparability.

Extending the validated own-history reallocation contrast to the advertising channel is economically distinct from the R&D version and untested in this archive, though xad is reported by a small and selected subset of firms so coverage and portfolio stability will need close scrutiny before any positive result is believed.

A single, well-diagnosed measurement change — substituting gross profit for revenue in the per-worker leg to separate rent generation from sales volume — that directly tests why the labor-productivity signal had a strong slope but no alpha, and is not reducible to the standard gross-profitability anomaly given the within-firm ranking and capital-deepening subtraction.

The dollar-weighted aggregation of capex and inventory build scaled by average assets is a genuine measurement improvement over the MIN-of-percentiles version and the expression matches the hypothesis, but it will likely be highly correlated with the existing capacity-push signal, so the incremental information should be reported explicitly.

The hypothesis is explicitly conditional ("most destructive when financed with outside capital") while the expression merely adds an issuance rank, so the construct is a portfolio blend of the archive's capacity-timing signal with the well-known net-external-financing/issuance anomaly rather than a test of the stated interaction.

This is the archive's OvercommitmentWhereKnowledgeEndowmentIsAbsent with MIN swapped for MUL on identical legs — a mechanical smoothing of the same construct rather than a substantively different mechanism, and the family's flat FMB slope is more plausibly a concentration-of-effect issue than a functional-form artifact.

Identical legs to the archive's OvercommitmentFundedFromOutsideCapital with only the aggregator changed, and since that version already delivers both a −4.9 FMB slope and a significant alpha, this is a cosmetic variant with little diagnostic value.

Same triple conjunction as AcquisitiveNonInnovatorsOvercommittingNow with MIN→MUL and a minor re-scaling of the R&D leg; a product of three rank legs also concentrates almost all variation in a small extreme cohort, so it is unlikely to fix the missing cross-sectional slope it claims to repair.

Testing whether the gating mechanism is symmetric on the long side is a genuinely different question rather than a sign flip of an existing signal, but the only cross-sectional leg is industry-relative R&D-to-sales, so a positive result will be hard to separate from the known R&D-intensity anomaly and will need that decomposition.

Replacing the own-history margin *position* with a fitted five-year margin *trend* is a substantive change in the economic content of the gate (structural erosion vs. cyclical dip), the expression matches the stated hypothesis, and both legs stay own-history so the construct is not a repackaged cross-sectional investment or profitability sort.

As a placebo gate the design logic is sound, but the gate double-counts the gross margin already embedded in the overcommitment leg and effectively tilts the short side toward low industry-relative gross profitability — a well-known published anomaly — so any strong result is uninformative about the intangibles claim it is meant to adjudicate.

This is a mechanical union of two already-tested archive signals (TotalPhysicalCommitmentAgainstMarginErosion and NetHardAssetCommitmentAgainstMarginErosion) whose legs are near-identical in construction, so it is a cosmetic consolidation unlikely to teach anything new about the mechanism beyond which of the two parents dominates.

Swapping the R&D-intensity gate for a knowledge-stock-share gate is a defensible attempt to distinguish stock composition from spending intensity, though the two gates are likely highly correlated so the discriminating power of the test may be modest.

Preserving the sign of the allocation contrast before weighting by the endowment converts a one-sided cohort screen into a genuine two-sided interaction, which is a substantive functional-form test with an internally consistent positive expected sign.

The three-year lag on the research gate is an economically motivated and genuinely new twist (harvest cohort rather than spending cohort), but changing the rent leg to gross profit per asset at the same time confounds attribution and edges toward the published gross-profitability channel.

Because the leg is a within-firm TS_RANK, adding a smooth, slow-moving R&D stock to the denominator will barely reorder the firm's own history — and for the many firms with no reported R&D the expression is literally unchanged — making this a near-null cosmetic variant of an archived signal.

The second leg is degenerate for non-R&D firms: coalescing xrd to zero before IND_ADJ makes their own-history rank track the negative of the industry R&D mean rather than any firm attribute, so a large fraction of the sample is sorted on an industry time trend, and the stated "full coverage" claim obscures this artifact.

This is a one-atom ablation of the archived KnowledgeRichCapitalRestraintWithMarginRepair (only the gate's 3-year lag differs) and sits strictly between two already-tested signals, so it is a cosmetic attribution variant rather than a new economic hypothesis.
